options.C: Karnataka has no seismic monitoring
options.D: Karnataka is entirely in Zone I

questions.explanation: Karnataka includes areas classified in Seismic Zone II and Zone III under the BIS seismic zoning map. The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) is the state's nodal agency for monitoring seismic activity. Its published geological-hazard information describes a network of permanent seismic monitoring stations across Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Explain the causes and effects of tsunamis. Which option is correct?

options.A: Tsunamis are caused by wind; effects are limited to the ocean surface
options.B: The most common cause is large shallow undersea earthquakes with significant vertical seabed displacement; landslides and volcanic activity can also generate tsunamis. Effects include coastal flooding and inundation, strong currents, drowning, injuries and deaths, destruction of buildings and infrastructure, erosion, saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater, damage to ports and fisheries, displacement of communities and economic disruption
options.C: Tsunamis are caused by tides; effects are only temporary
options.D: Tsunamis are caused by meteorite impacts only; effects are limited to coastal erosion

questions.explanation: Large, shallow undersea earthquakes that cause significant vertical displacement of the seabed are the most common cause of major destructive tsunamis. Submarine landslides and volcanic activity can also generate tsunamis. Major effects include coastal flooding and inundation, strong currents, drowning, injuries and deaths, destruction of buildings and infrastructure, erosion, saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater, damage to ports and fisheries, displacement of communities and economic disruption.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a natural warning sign of a possible tsunami?

options.A: A strong or long-lasting coastal earthquake
options.B: An unusual rapid rise or fall of sea level
options.C: A loud ocean roar
options.D: Clear skies and calm weather

questions.explanation: Natural warning signs of a possible tsunami include a strong or long-lasting coastal earthquake, an unusual rapid rise or fall of sea level, and a loud ocean roar. Clear skies and calm weather are not tsunami warning signs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor that influences earthquake damage?

options.A: Magnitude and depth
options.B: Local soil and geological conditions
options.C: Building design and construction quality
options.D: The colour of the buildings

questions.explanation: Magnitude, depth, distance from the source, duration and frequency content of shaking, local soil and geological conditions, building design and construction quality, population density, time of occurrence and preparedness all influence damage. The colour of buildings is not a factor.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of earthquake based on cause?

options.D: Tidal earthquake

questions.explanation: Major causes or types of earthquakes include tectonic earthquakes, volcanic earthquakes, collapse earthquakes and human-induced (induced) earthquakes. 'Tidal earthquake' is not a recognised type in this classification.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a human activity that can cause induced seismicity?

options.B: Mining

questions.explanation: Human-induced or induced seismicity can result from activities such as reservoir impoundment, mining, fluid injection or extraction, and some underground engineering operations. Planting trees is not associated with induced seismicity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Richter scale is INCORRECT?

options.A: It is a logarithmic scale
options.B: A one-unit increase corresponds to ten times the recorded wave amplitude
options.C: The energy released increases by roughly 32 times for each whole-number magnitude step
options.D: It is the most suitable scale for all very large and distant earthquakes

questions.explanation: The original local magnitude scale can saturate for large earthquakes and is not ideal for very large or distant events. Modern reporting generally favours moment magnitude for large earthquakes. Options A, B and C are correct statements about the Richter scale.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale is INCORRECT?

options.A: It has 12 levels, from I to XII
options.B: It describes the effects of earthquake shaking at a particular location
options.C: It measures the total energy released at the earthquake focus
options.D: The same earthquake can have different Mercalli intensities at different locations

questions.explanation: The Mercalli intensity scale does NOT measure the total energy released at the focus. It describes the observed effects and shaking at a location. Options A, B and D are correct statements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a surface wave?

options.A: Love wave
options.B: Rayleigh wave
options.C: P-wave
options.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: Love waves and Rayleigh waves are surface waves. P-waves are body waves (primary or compressional seismic waves).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a body wave?

options.A: P-wave
options.B: S-wave
options.C: Love wave
options.D: None of the above

questions.explanation: P-waves and S-waves are body waves. Love waves are surface waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about P-waves is INCORRECT?

options.A: They are the fastest seismic body waves
options.B: They travel through solids, liquids and gases
options.C: Particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
options.D: They are generally recorded first by a seismograph

questions.explanation: In P-waves, particles vibrate back and forth parallel to the direction in which the wave travels, producing alternating compression and expansion. Vibrating perpendicular to the direction of propagation is characteristic of S-waves, not P-waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about S-waves is INCORRECT?

options.A: They are slower than P-waves
options.B: They can travel through liquids
options.C: Particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
options.D: Their absence through Earth's liquid outer core is important evidence that the outer core is liquid

questions.explanation: S-waves cannot propagate through liquids because liquids do not support the shear rigidity required for shear waves. Options A, C and D are correct statements about S-waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Love waves is INCORRECT?

options.A: They are surface waves
options.B: They produce mainly horizontal side-to-side shear motion
options.C: They produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion similar to ocean waves
options.D: They generally travel perpendicular to the direction of propagation

questions.explanation: Love waves produce mainly horizontal side-to-side shear motion, generally perpendicular to the direction of propagation, without the vertical rolling motion characteristic of Rayleigh waves. The rolling, elliptical particle motion similar to ocean waves is characteristic of Rayleigh waves, not Love waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Rayleigh waves is INCORRECT?

options.A: They are surface waves
options.B: They produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion
options.C: They produce only horizontal side-to-side motion
options.D: Their motion includes both vertical and horizontal components

questions.explanation: Rayleigh waves produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion that includes both vertical and horizontal components, similar in broad appearance to ocean waves. They do NOT produce only horizontal side-to-side motion; that is characteristic of Love waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic zoning in India is INCORRECT?

options.A: The BIS framework classifies India into four zones: II, III, IV and V
options.B: Zone V is the highest seismic-hazard zone
options.C: Zone I is the highest seismic-hazard zone
options.D: Zone II is the lowest seismic-hazard zone in the four-zone classification

questions.explanation: Zone I is not used in the current four-zone classification. Zone V is the highest seismic-hazard zone and Zone II is the lowest in the four-zone scheme.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's seismic zones is INCORRECT?

options.A: Karnataka includes areas in Zone II and Zone III
options.B: Some Karnataka districts span both Zone II and Zone III
options.C: Karnataka has areas in Zone IV and Zone V
options.D: A lower seismic zone does not mean Karnataka is earthquake-free

questions.explanation: Karnataka includes areas classified in Seismic Zone II and Zone III under the BIS seismic zoning map. There are no Zone IV or Zone V areas in the official district-wise summary cited by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunamis is INCORRECT?

options.A: A tsunami is usually a series of waves
options.B: The first tsunami wave is always the largest
options.C: In deep water, tsunami waves may have low wave height but very long wavelengths
options.D: A tsunami involves the movement of a large water column

questions.explanation: The first tsunami wave is NOT necessarily the largest. A tsunami is a wave train whose waves interact with ocean-basin and coastal geometry, and later waves can be larger or produce stronger currents than the first.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami causes is INCORRECT?

options.A: Large shallow undersea earthquakes with significant vertical seabed displacement are the most common cause of major destructive tsunamis
options.B: Submarine landslides can generate tsunamis
options.C: Volcanic eruptions can generate tsunamis
options.D: All undersea earthquakes generate tsunamis

questions.explanation: Not all undersea earthquakes generate tsunamis. Many are too small, too deep, or produce mostly horizontal displacement. Tsunami generation is especially associated with large shallow earthquakes that cause substantial vertical seabed movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake preparedness is INCORRECT?

options.A: During indoor shaking, you should Drop, Cover and Hold On
options.B: You should use elevators during an earthquake to evacuate quickly
options.C: After an earthquake, you should expect aftershocks
options.D: If near the coast after strong shaking, you should move to higher ground

questions.explanation: You should NOT use elevators during shaking or immediately after an earthquake. Use stairs only after shaking stops and when the route is safe. Options A, C and D are correct preparedness actions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake early-warning systems is INCORRECT?

options.A: They detect faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source
options.B: They can provide seconds to tens of seconds of warning in some situations
options.C: They provide reliable long-term prediction of the exact date, location and magnitude of future earthquakes
options.D: They may not provide warning close to the epicentre

questions.explanation: Earthquake early-warning systems do NOT provide long-term prediction. They detect faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source and send alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives. They provide seconds to tens of seconds in some situations and may not provide warning close to the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake magnitude and intensity is INCORRECT?

options.A: Magnitude estimates the size of the earthquake source
options.B: Intensity describes the local effects of shaking at a site
options.C: One earthquake has one principal magnitude estimate but can have many intensity values across the affected region
options.D: Magnitude and intensity are interchangeable terms

questions.explanation: Magnitude and intensity are NOT interchangeable. Magnitude estimates the size of the earthquake source; intensity describes the local effects of shaking at a site. One earthquake has one principal magnitude estimate but can have many intensity values across the affected region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the focus and epicentre is INCORRECT?

options.A: The focus is inside the Earth
options.B: The epicentre is on the Earth's surface directly above the focus
options.C: The epicentre is always the place of maximum damage
options.D: Focal depth is the vertical distance from the surface to the focus

questions.explanation: The epicentre is NOT always the place of maximum damage. Local soil amplification, rupture direction, depth, building vulnerability and other factors can cause maximum damage away from the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic waves is INCORRECT?

options.A: P-waves are faster than S-waves
options.B: S-waves are faster than surface waves in typical earthquake records
options.C: Surface waves travel through Earth's interior
options.D: S-waves cannot travel through liquids

questions.explanation: Surface waves travel along or near the Earth's surface, NOT through Earth's interior. Body waves travel through Earth's interior. Options A, B and D are correct statements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the moment magnitude scale is INCORRECT?

options.A: It is based on seismic moment
options.B: It reflects the rigidity of rocks, the area of the fault that slipped and the average amount of slip
options.C: It saturates for very large earthquakes in the same way as older magnitude scales
options.D: It provides a consistent measure across a wide range of earthquake sizes

questions.explanation: The moment magnitude scale does NOT saturate in the same way as older magnitude scales for very large events. It is physically related to the size of the earthquake source and provides a consistent measure across a wide range of earthquake sizes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami is INCORRECT?

options.A: It was generated by a great undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra
options.B: It occurred on 26 December 2004
options.C: It affected only Indonesia
options.D: It affected India's east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.explanation: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami affected many countries around the Indian Ocean, including India's east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. It did not affect only Indonesia.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the distribution of India's land area among seismic zones is INCORRECT?

options.A: About 11% of India's land area is in Zone V
options.B: About 18% of India's land area is in Zone IV
options.C: About 30% of India's land area is in Zone III
options.D: About 50% of India's land area is in Zone V

questions.explanation: A Ministry of Earth Sciences parliamentary answer in 2022 gave approximate figures of about 11% in Zone V, 18% in Zone IV, 30% in Zone III and the remaining area in Zone II. About 50% in Zone V is incorrect.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami run-up and inundation is INCORRECT?

options.A: Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land
options.B: Inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline
options.C: Run-up and inundation mean the same thing
options.D: Both run-up and inundation are important measures of tsunami impact

questions.explanation: Run-up and inundation are different concepts. Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land. Inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake-resistant construction is INCORRECT?

options.A: It aims to improve structural strength, ductility, connections and overall performance
options.B: Ductility helps structures dissipate earthquake energy
options.C: Retrofitting is the strengthening or modification of an existing building to improve its resistance to earthquake shaking
options.D: Earthquake-resistant construction guarantees that buildings will never suffer any damage

questions.explanation: Earthquake-resistant construction aims to resist expected earthquake forces without unacceptable collapse or loss of life. It does NOT guarantee that buildings will never suffer any damage. Options A, B and C are correct statements.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake prediction is INCORRECT?

options.A: Scientists can estimate seismic hazard and probabilities over time
options.B: Scientists can monitor earthquakes and issue alerts after an earthquake has begun
options.C: Scientists can reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake
options.D: Earthquake early-warning systems provide seconds to tens of seconds of warning in some situations

questions.explanation: Scientists cannot reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake. They can estimate seismic hazard and probabilities over time, monitor earthquakes and issue alerts after an earthquake has begun.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on agriculture is INCORRECT?

options.A: Saltwater can contaminate fields and groundwater
options.B: Tsunamis can damage crops and reduce soil productivity
options.C: Tsunamis always improve soil fertility
options.D: Tsunamis can harm livestock

questions.explanation: Tsunamis do NOT always improve soil fertility. Saltwater can contaminate fields and groundwater, damage crops, reduce soil productivity and harm livestock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on the environment is INCORRECT?

options.A: They can erode beaches and dunes
options.B: They can move large amounts of sediment
options.C: They can damage mangroves and coastal habitats
options.D: They have no effect on coastal ecosystems

questions.explanation: Tsunamis CAN affect coastal ecosystems. They can erode beaches and dunes, move large amounts of sediment, damage mangroves and coastal habitats, spread debris and pollutants, and alter coastal ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2022 MoES district-wise seismic zone table for Karnataka is INCORRECT?

options.A: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura and Uttara Kannada contain Zone III areas
options.B: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Raichur and Koppal were listed as Zone II only
options.C: Udupi is listed as Zone III
options.D: All districts of Karnataka are entirely in Zone III

questions.explanation: Not all districts of Karnataka are entirely in Zone III. Several districts span Zone II and Zone III, and some districts were listed as Zone II only. The 2022 MoES table lists specific districts with Zone III areas and others as Zone II only.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on ports and coastal infrastructure is INCORRECT?

options.A: Powerful currents can damage ships and harbours
options.B: Debris impact can damage roads, bridges and railways
options.C: Flooding and rapid water-level changes can damage power systems and communication networks
options.D: Ports and coastal infrastructure are immune to tsunami damage

questions.explanation: Ports and coastal infrastructure are NOT immune to tsunami damage. Powerful currents, debris impact, flooding and rapid water-level changes can damage ships, harbours, roads, bridges, railways, power systems and communication networks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami warning is INCORRECT?

options.A: INCOIS operates India's tsunami early-warning capability
options.B: People should wait for an official warning after a strong coastal earthquake before evacuating
options.C: A tsunami consists of multiple waves and strong currents may persist
options.D: People should remain in safe locations until the competent authority officially declares the threat over

questions.explanation: People should NOT wait for an official warning after a strong coastal earthquake. If a person is in a coastal area and experiences strong or prolonged earthquake shaking, they should move immediately to higher ground or inland when safe to do so.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake preparedness before an earthquake is INCORRECT?

options.A: Secure heavy furniture and appliances
options.B: Keep heavy objects on lower shelves
options.C: Store heavy objects above beds and seating areas
options.D: Practise Drop, Cover and Hold On

questions.explanation: You should NOT store heavy objects above beds and seating areas. Keep breakable and heavy items on lower shelves and avoid storing heavy objects above beds and seating areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what to do during an earthquake is INCORRECT?

options.A: Drop to hands and knees
options.B: Take cover under a sturdy table or desk if available
options.C: Run outside immediately while the building is shaking
options.D: Protect the head and neck

questions.explanation: You should NOT run outside while the building is shaking. Drop, Cover and Hold On indoors; stay away from windows, glass, exterior walls and heavy objects.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what to do after an earthquake is INCORRECT?

options.A: Expect aftershocks
options.B: Check for injuries and provide first aid if safe
options.C: Enter visibly damaged buildings immediately to retrieve belongings
options.D: Check for gas leaks, fire and electrical hazards

questions.explanation: You should NOT enter visibly damaged buildings until authorities or qualified personnel declare them safe. Do not enter unsafe buildings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about driving during an earthquake is INCORRECT?

options.A: Pull over carefully in a safe location
options.B: Stop away from bridges, flyovers, buildings, trees and power lines
options.C: Speed up to cross bridges quickly
options.D: Remain in the vehicle until shaking stops

questions.explanation: You should NOT speed up to cross bridges quickly during an earthquake. Pull over carefully in a safe location away from bridges, flyovers, buildings, trees and power lines. Stop, remain in the vehicle until shaking stops.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the seismograph and seismogram is INCORRECT?

options.A: A seismograph is an instrument or recording system used to detect and record ground motion
options.B: A seismogram is the recorded trace or digital record of ground motion
options.C: A seismograph directly measures earthquake magnitude without any calculations
options.D: Modern instruments use electronic sensors and digital data acquisition

questions.explanation: A seismograph does NOT directly measure earthquake magnitude. It records ground motion. Magnitude is calculated from recorded wave amplitudes and other parameters, with corrections for distance, frequency, instrument response and, depending on the scale, seismic moment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic wave speeds is INCORRECT?

options.A: P-waves are the fastest seismic body waves
options.B: S-waves are slower than P-waves
options.C: Surface waves are generally faster than body waves
options.D: Surface waves are generally slower than body waves but can produce large-amplitude shaking

questions.explanation: Surface waves are generally SLOWER than body waves, not faster. They can produce large-amplitude shaking and substantial damage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic zoning in India is INCORRECT?

options.A: Seismic zoning divides a region into areas according to expected levels of earthquake ground shaking or seismic hazard
options.B: Seismic zoning helps guide earthquake-resistant construction and risk reduction
options.C: A seismic zone tells the exact probability or date of an earthquake
options.D: Zone II does not mean that earthquakes are impossible there

questions.explanation: A seismic zone does NOT tell the exact probability or date of an earthquake. Seismic zoning is a planning classification of expected hazard, not a prediction of when or exactly where an earthquake will occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about local shaking within a seismic zone is INCORRECT?

options.A: Local soil conditions can produce different levels of shaking within the same zone
options.B: Sediment thickness can affect shaking intensity
options.C: Topography and basin effects can influence shaking
options.D: Every location within one seismic zone experiences identical shaking

questions.explanation: Every location within one seismic zone does NOT experience identical shaking. Local soil, sediment thickness, topography, basin effects, fault proximity and building conditions can produce different levels of shaking within the same zone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2022 MoES table on Karnataka districts is INCORRECT?

options.A: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Uttara Kannada and Shivamogga contain Zone III and Zone II portions
options.B: Udupi is listed as Zone III
options.C: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Raichur and Koppal were listed as Zone II only
options.D: All districts of Karnataka contain only Zone V areas

questions.explanation: No district of Karnataka contains Zone V areas according to the 2022 MoES table. Karnataka includes only Zone II and Zone III areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on communication is INCORRECT?

options.A: Tsunamis can damage communication networks
options.B: Using text messages is recommended after an earthquake to reduce congestion on voice networks
options.C: Spreading rumours and unverified messages is helpful during a disaster
options.D: Listening to official updates is recommended

questions.explanation: Spreading rumours and unverified messages is NOT helpful. Listen to official updates and do not spread rumours or unverified messages.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on coastal flooding is INCORRECT?

options.A: Tsunamis can cause coastal flooding and inundation
options.B: Strong currents associated with tsunamis can be dangerous
options.C: Tsunami flooding cannot reach far inland under any circumstances
options.D: Low-lying coastal plains, river mouths and bays may allow water to penetrate considerable distances

questions.explanation: Tsunami flooding CAN reach far inland. The inland reach depends on wave characteristics and coastal topography. Low-lying coastal plains, river mouths and bays may allow water to penetrate considerable distances.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the west coast of India and tsunamis is INCORRECT?

options.A: The west coast is not immune to tsunami hazards
options.B: Tsunami risk depends on the location and characteristics of the generating event and the propagation path
options.C: Only the east coast of India can experience tsunamis
options.D: Although exposure differs from the east coast, the west coast can experience tsunamis

questions.explanation: It is INCORRECT that only the east coast of India can experience tsunamis. Although exposure differs from the east coast, the west coast is not immune to tsunami hazards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake early-warning systems is INCORRECT?

options.A: They detect faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source
options.B: They send alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives
options.C: They provide long-term prediction of the exact date, location and magnitude of future earthquakes
options.D: They may not provide warning close to the epicentre

questions.explanation: Earthquake early-warning systems do NOT provide long-term prediction. They detect faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source and send alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives. They provide seconds to tens of seconds in some situations, not long-term prediction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the sources and further reading for earthquakes is INCORRECT?

options.A: The National Centre for Seismology, Ministry of Earth Sciences, provides earthquake information and official preparedness guidance
options.B: The Ministry of Earth Sciences published a Rajya Sabha answer on earthquake threat and Karnataka seismic zones on 22 December 2022
options.C: The Karnataka State Disaster Management Authority publishes the Karnataka State Disaster Management Plan
options.D: The Bureau of Indian Standards does not publish any seismic design or zoning framework

questions.explanation: The Bureau of Indian Standards DOES publish seismic design and zoning frameworks, including IS 1893. Consult the applicable current edition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the elastic rebound theory is INCORRECT?

options.A: Rocks on either side of a locked fault gradually deform as tectonic stress builds
options.B: When the fault ruptures, the rocks spring partly back towards an undeformed state
options.C: The release of stored energy generates an earthquake
options.D: The theory states that rocks never deform before an earthquake

questions.explanation: The elastic rebound theory states that rocks on either side of a locked fault DO gradually deform as tectonic stress builds. When the fault ruptures, the rocks spring partly back towards an undeformed state, releasing stored energy and generating an earthquake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake damage and focal depth is INCORRECT?

options.A: When other factors are similar, a shallow earthquake generally releases energy closer to the surface
options.B: Strong shaking from a shallow earthquake may occur near the source
options.C: Actual damage from a shallow earthquake depends on magnitude, geology, buildings and distance
options.D: Deep earthquakes always cause more damage than shallow earthquakes

questions.explanation: Deep earthquakes do NOT always cause more damage than shallow earthquakes. When other factors are similar, a shallow earthquake generally releases energy closer to the surface, so strong shaking may occur near the source. Actual damage still depends on magnitude, geology, buildings and distance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the relationship between amplitude and energy on the Richter scale is INCORRECT?

options.A: A one-unit increase corresponds to ten times the recorded wave amplitude
options.B: The energy released increases by roughly 32 times for each whole-number magnitude step
options.C: A magnitude 6 earthquake releases ten times the energy of a magnitude 5 earthquake
options.D: The recorded wave amplitude is about ten times greater for a one-unit increase

questions.explanation: A magnitude 6 earthquake does NOT release ten times the energy of a magnitude 5 earthquake. The recorded wave amplitude is about ten times greater for a one-unit increase, while the energy release is approximately 32 times greater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the epicentre and maximum damage is INCORRECT?

options.A: The epicentre may be near the area of strongest shaking
options.B: Local soil amplification can cause maximum damage away from the epicentre
options.C: Rupture direction can cause maximum damage away from the epicentre
options.D: The epicentre is always the place of maximum damage regardless of other factors

questions.explanation: The epicentre is NOT always the place of maximum damage. Local soil amplification, rupture direction, depth, building vulnerability and other factors can cause maximum damage away from the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale and energy is INCORRECT?

options.A: It describes the observed effects and shaking at a location
options.B: It does not measure the total energy released at the earthquake source
options.C: It measures the total energy released at the focus
options.D: The same earthquake can have different Mercalli intensities at different locations

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale does NOT measure the total energy released at the focus. It describes the observed effects and shaking at a location.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami warning and the first wave is INCORRECT?

options.A: A tsunami consists of multiple waves
options.B: Strong currents may persist after the first wave
options.C: The danger is over after the first wave
options.D: People should remain in safe locations until the competent authority officially declares the threat over

questions.explanation: The danger is NOT over after the first wave. A tsunami consists of multiple waves and strong currents may persist. People should remain in safe locations until the competent authority officially declares the threat over.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the role of KSNDMC is INCORRECT?

options.A: It is the Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre
options.B: It is the state's nodal agency for monitoring seismic activity
options.C: Its published geological-hazard information describes a network of permanent seismic monitoring stations across Karnataka
options.D: It operates India's tsunami early-warning system

questions.explanation: KSNDMC does NOT operate India's tsunami early-warning system. India's tsunami early-warning capability is operated by INCOIS. KSNDMC is Karnataka's nodal agency for monitoring seismic activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on ports is INCORRECT?

options.A: Powerful currents can damage ships and harbours
options.B: Debris impact can damage roads, bridges and railways
options.C: Flooding and rapid water-level changes can damage power systems and communication networks
options.D: Ports and coastal infrastructure are completely immune to tsunami damage

questions.explanation: Ports and coastal infrastructure are NOT completely immune to tsunami damage. Powerful currents, debris impact, flooding and rapid water-level changes can damage ships, harbours, roads, bridges, railways, power systems and communication networks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on agriculture is INCORRECT?

options.A: Saltwater can contaminate fields and groundwater
options.B: Tsunamis can damage crops and reduce soil productivity
options.C: Tsunamis always improve soil fertility
options.D: Tsunamis can harm livestock

questions.explanation: Tsunamis do NOT always improve soil fertility. Saltwater can contaminate fields and groundwater, damage crops, reduce soil productivity and harm livestock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis on the environment is INCORRECT?

options.A: They can erode beaches and dunes
options.B: They can move large amounts of sediment
options.C: They can damage mangroves and coastal habitats
options.D: They have no effect on coastal ecosystems

questions.explanation: Tsunamis CAN affect coastal ecosystems. They can erode beaches and dunes, move large amounts of sediment, damage mangroves and coastal habitats, spread debris and pollutants, and alter coastal ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2022 MoES district-wise seismic zone table for Karnataka is INCORRECT?

options.A: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura and Uttara Kannada contain Zone III areas
options.B: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Raichur and Koppal were listed as Zone II only
options.C: Udupi is listed as Zone III
options.D: All districts of Karnataka are entirely in Zone III

questions.explanation: Not all districts of Karnataka are entirely in Zone III. Several districts span Zone II and Zone III, and some districts were listed as Zone II only.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami warning and the first wave is INCORRECT?

options.A: A tsunami consists of multiple waves
options.B: Strong currents may persist after the first wave
options.C: The danger is over after the first wave
options.D: People should remain in safe locations until the competent authority officially declares the threat over

questions.explanation: The danger is NOT over after the first wave. A tsunami consists of multiple waves and strong currents may persist.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which seismic zone is NOT used in India's current four-zone BIS classification?

options.A: Zone II
options.B: Zone III
options.C: Zone IV
options.D: Zone I

questions.explanation: Zone I is not used in the current four-zone classification. The BIS framework classifies India into Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV and Zone V.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of seismic wave arrival at a recording station?

options.A: S-wave, P-wave, surface waves
options.B: P-wave, S-wave, surface waves
options.C: Surface waves, P-wave, S-wave
options.D: P-wave, surface waves, S-wave

questions.explanation: P-waves arrive first (fastest), then S-waves, then surface waves (slowest but often most damaging).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic wave with its particle motion?

options.A: P-wave: perpendicular to travel direction
options.B: S-wave: parallel to travel direction
options.C: P-wave: parallel to travel direction; S-wave: perpendicular to travel direction
options.D: Rayleigh wave: only horizontal side-to-side motion

questions.explanation: P-waves: particles vibrate parallel to the direction of wave travel (compression/expansion). S-waves: particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation (shear).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic wave with its ability to travel through mediums?

options.A: P-wave: solids only
options.B: S-wave: solids, liquids and gases
options.C: P-wave: solids, liquids and gases; S-wave: solids only
options.D: Both P and S waves travel through all mediums

questions.explanation: P-waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases. S-waves cannot propagate through liquids because liquids do not support shear rigidity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an instrument with its function?

options.A: Seismograph: records ground motion
options.B: Seismogram: the sensing component of a seismograph
options.C: Accelerograph: measures tsunami height
options.D: Seismometer: the recorded trace of ground motion

questions.explanation: A seismograph is an instrument or recording system used to detect and record ground motion. A seismogram is the recorded trace. A seismometer is the sensor that measures ground motion. An accelerograph records ground acceleration.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a magnitude/intensity scale with its basis?

options.A: Richter scale: seismic moment
options.B: Moment magnitude: recorded wave amplitudes in southern California
options.C: Modified Mercalli: observed effects and damage at a location
options.D: Moment magnitude: observed shaking and damage

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale describes the effects of earthquake shaking at a particular location based on human observations, effects on objects, and damage to structures. The Richter scale is based on recorded seismic-wave amplitudes. Moment magnitude is based on seismic moment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic zone with its hazard category in India's four-zone scheme?

options.A: Zone II: very high hazard
options.B: Zone III: low hazard
options.C: Zone IV: high hazard
options.D: Zone V: lowest hazard

questions.explanation: Zone II: low; Zone III: moderate; Zone IV: high; Zone V: very high (highest hazard category).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami term with its meaning?

options.A: Run-up: horizontal penetration of water inland
options.B: Inundation: maximum vertical height reached by water on land
options.C: Run-up: maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land
options.D: Inundation: speed of tsunami waves in deep water

questions.explanation: Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land. Inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami cause with its description?

options.A: Undersea earthquake: large mass moves into or beneath water
options.B: Submarine landslide: sudden vertical movement of seabed
options.C: Volcanic activity: explosion, collapse or material entering water
options.D: Meteorite impact: most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis

questions.explanation: Volcanic activity can generate tsunamis through explosion, collapse or material entering water. Undersea earthquake involves sudden vertical movement of seabed. Submarine landslide involves a large mass moving into or beneath water. Meteorite impact is extremely rare.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami effect with its description?

options.A: Agriculture: damage to ports and fisheries
options.B: Environment: saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater
options.C: Infrastructure: erosion of beaches and dunes
options.D: Agriculture: saltwater contamination of fields and groundwater, damage to crops, reduced soil productivity and harm to livestock

questions.explanation: Agriculture effects include saltwater contamination of fields and groundwater, damage to crops, reduced soil productivity and harm to livestock. Environment effects include erosion of beaches and dunes, sediment movement, damage to mangroves and coastal habitats. Infrastructure effects include damage to ports, fisheries, roads, bridges, railways, power systems and communication networks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a preparedness action with its timing?

options.A: Before: Drop, Cover and Hold On
options.B: During: secure heavy furniture and appliances
options.C: After: expect aftershocks
options.D: During: check for gas leaks

questions.explanation: After an earthquake: expect aftershocks. Before: secure heavy furniture and appliances. During: Drop, Cover and Hold On. Checking for gas leaks is an after-earthquake action.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an earthquake type with its cause?

options.A: Tectonic earthquake: magma movement and volcanic activity
options.B: Volcanic earthquake: sudden movement along a fault due to tectonic stress
options.C: Induced earthquake: human activities that alter stress or pore-fluid pressure
options.D: Collapse earthquake: plate boundary movement

questions.explanation: Induced earthquakes are triggered or influenced by human activities that alter stress or pore-fluid pressure in the Earth's crust. Tectonic earthquakes result from fault movement associated with plate tectonics. Volcanic earthquakes are associated with magma movement and volcanic activity. Collapse earthquakes may occur when underground cavities or mines collapse.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic wave with its other name?

options.A: P-wave: shear wave
options.B: S-wave: compressional wave
options.C: P-wave: primary wave or compressional wave
options.D: S-wave: surface wave

questions.explanation: P-waves are also called primary or compressional seismic waves. S-waves are also called secondary or shear seismic waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic zone with areas broadly associated with it?

options.A: Zone V: only the Deccan Plateau
options.B: Zone V: much of the northeastern region, parts of the Himalayan belt, the Rann of Kutch, parts of northern Bihar and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
options.C: Zone IV: only coastal Kerala
options.D: Zone II: only the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

questions.explanation: Zone V includes much of the northeastern region, parts of the Himalayan belt, the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat, parts of northern Bihar and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an MMI level range with its description?

options.A: I: total destruction
options.B: II-III: weak shaking; felt by some people, especially indoors
options.C: IV-V: extreme to catastrophic effects
options.D: X-XII: light shaking with no damage

questions.explanation: MMI II-III: weak shaking; felt by some people, especially indoors. MMI I: not felt except by very few. MMI IV-V: light to moderate shaking. MMI X-XII: extreme to catastrophic effects.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an MMI level range with its description?

options.A: VI-VII: strong to very strong shaking; slight to moderate damage may occur
options.B: VIII-IX: weak shaking felt indoors
options.C: X-XII: light to moderate shaking
options.D: IV-V: total destruction

questions.explanation: MMI VI-VII: strong to very strong shaking; slight to moderate damage may occur. MMI VIII-IX: severe to violent shaking; considerable damage in vulnerable structures. MMI X-XII: extreme to catastrophic effects. MMI IV-V: light to moderate shaking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches an MMI level range with its description?

options.A: VIII-IX: severe to violent shaking; considerable damage in vulnerable structures
options.B: X-XII: weak shaking felt by some people
options.C: VI-VII: not felt at all
options.D: II-III: total destruction

questions.explanation: MMI VIII-IX: severe to violent shaking; considerable damage in vulnerable structures. MMI X-XII: extreme to catastrophic effects. MMI VI-VII: strong to very strong shaking. MMI II-III: weak shaking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a term with its definition?

options.A: Focus: surface point directly above the hypocentre
options.B: Epicentre: point inside Earth where rupture starts
options.C: Focal depth: vertical distance from the Earth's surface to the earthquake focus
options.D: Fault: a type of seismic wave

questions.explanation: Focal depth is the vertical distance from the Earth's surface to the earthquake focus. Focus (hypocentre) is the point inside Earth where rupture starts. Epicentre is the surface point directly above the focus. A fault is a fracture or fracture zone along which rock displacement occurs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a term with its definition?

options.A: Aftershock: earthquake that precedes a larger earthquake
options.B: Foreshock: smaller or subsequent earthquake following a larger event
options.C: Aftershock: smaller or subsequent earthquake following a larger event in the same affected region
options.D: Foreshock: the point inside Earth where rupture starts

questions.explanation: An aftershock is a smaller or subsequent earthquake following a larger event in the same affected region. A foreshock is an earthquake that precedes a larger earthquake in the same region; it is identified as a foreshock only in retrospect.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic wave with its key feature?

options.A: P-wave: shear; travels through solids only; arrives second
options.B: S-wave: compressional; travels through solids, liquids and gases; arrives first
options.C: Love wave: horizontal side-to-side shear; travels along surface; arrives after body waves
options.D: Rayleigh wave: horizontal side-to-side shear only

questions.explanation: Love waves produce horizontal side-to-side shear motion, travel along the surface and arrive after body waves. P-waves are compressional, travel through solids, liquids and gases, and arrive first. S-waves are shear, travel through solids only, and arrive second. Rayleigh waves produce rolling elliptical motion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic wave with its key feature?

options.A: Rayleigh wave: rolling elliptical motion including vertical and horizontal components; travels along surface; arrives after body waves
options.B: Love wave: rolling elliptical motion
options.C: P-wave: shear motion perpendicular to travel direction
options.D: S-wave: compressional motion parallel to travel direction

questions.explanation: Rayleigh waves produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion that includes both vertical and horizontal components, travel along the surface and arrive after body waves. Love waves produce horizontal side-to-side shear motion. P-waves are compressional. S-waves are shear.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a magnitude/intensity scale with its key feature?

options.A: Richter scale: based on seismic moment; preferred for large earthquakes
options.B: Moment magnitude: local magnitude scale developed in 1935
options.C: Modified Mercalli: 12 levels; describes observed effects at a location
options.D: Moment magnitude: 12 levels; describes observed damage

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale has 12 levels and describes the observed effects of earthquake shaking at a particular location. The Richter scale is the local magnitude scale developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935. Moment magnitude is based on seismic moment and is preferred for large earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a seismic zone with its hazard category?

options.A: Zone II: moderate hazard
options.B: Zone III: low hazard
options.C: Zone IV: high hazard
options.D: Zone V: lowest hazard

questions.explanation: Zone II: low; Zone III: moderate; Zone IV: high; Zone V: very high (highest hazard category).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami term with its meaning?

options.A: Inundation: maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land
options.B: Run-up: horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline
options.C: Inundation: horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline
options.D: Run-up: speed of tsunami waves in deep water

questions.explanation: Inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline. Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami cause with its typical note?

options.A: Undersea earthquake: can produce very large local waves
options.B: Submarine/coastal landslide: most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis
options.C: Undersea earthquake: most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis
options.D: Meteorite impact: most common cause of tsunamis

questions.explanation: Undersea earthquake with sudden vertical movement of seabed is the most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis. Submarine/coastal landslides can produce very large local waves. Meteorite impacts are extremely rare.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami cause with its typical note?

options.A: Submarine/coastal landslide: can produce very large local waves
options.B: Volcanic activity: most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis
options.C: Undersea earthquake: extremely rare
options.D: Meteorite impact: can produce very large local waves

questions.explanation: Submarine/coastal landslides can produce very large local waves. Undersea earthquakes are the most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis. Volcanic activity may generate local or regional tsunamis. Meteorite impacts are extremely rare.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami cause with its typical note?

options.A: Volcanic activity: may generate local or regional tsunamis
options.B: Undersea earthquake: extremely rare
options.C: Submarine landslide: most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis
options.D: Meteorite impact: most common cause of tsunamis

questions.explanation: Volcanic activity may generate local or regional tsunamis. Undersea earthquakes are the most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis. Submarine landslides can produce very large local waves. Meteorite impacts are extremely rare.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches a tsunami cause with its typical note?

options.A: Meteorite impact: extremely rare
options.B: Undersea earthquake: extremely rare
options.C: Volcanic activity: most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis
options.D: Submarine landslide: extremely rare

questions.explanation: Meteorite impacts that generate tsunamis are extremely rare. Undersea earthquakes are the most common cause of major ocean-wide tsunamis. Volcanic activity may generate local or regional tsunamis. Submarine landslides can produce very large local waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the correct order of the three main steps of Drop, Cover and Hold On?

options.A: Cover, Drop, Hold On
options.B: Drop to hands and knees, take cover under a sturdy table or desk, hold on to the shelter until shaking stops
options.C: Hold On, Drop, Cover
options.D: Run outside, Drop, Cover

questions.explanation: Drop, Cover and Hold On: Drop to hands and knees; take cover under a sturdy table or desk if available; protect the head and neck; hold on to the shelter until shaking stops.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the 2022 MoES parliamentary answer, which of the following Karnataka districts contains Zone III areas?

options.A: Bidar
options.B: Raichur
options.C: Udupi
options.D: Koppal

questions.explanation: Udupi is listed as Zone III in the 2022 MoES table. Bidar, Raichur and Koppal were listed as Zone II only.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the 2022 MoES parliamentary answer, which of the following Karnataka districts was listed as Zone II only?

options.A: Belagavi
options.B: Bagalkot
options.C: Kalaburagi
options.D: Shivamogga

questions.explanation: Kalaburagi (then Gulbarga) was listed as Zone II only in the 2022 MoES table. Belagavi, Bagalkot and Shivamogga contain Zone III areas (often alongside Zone II portions).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the 2022 MoES parliamentary answer, which of the following Karnataka districts contains Zone III areas?

options.A: Dharwad
options.B: Haveri
options.C: Dakshina Kannada
options.D: Gadag

questions.explanation: Dakshina Kannada is listed as containing Zone III areas (alongside Zone II portions) in the 2022 MoES table. Dharwad, Haveri and Gadag were listed as Zone II only.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: According to the 2022 MoES parliamentary answer, which of the following Karnataka districts was listed as Zone II only?

options.A: Chikkamagaluru
options.B: Bengaluru
options.C: Kolar
options.D: Kodagu

questions.explanation: Kolar was listed as Zone II only in the 2022 MoES table. Chikkamagaluru, Bengaluru and Kodagu contain Zone III areas (often alongside Zone II portions).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as containing Zone III areas in the 2022 MoES table for Karnataka?

options.A: Mysuru
options.B: Chamarajanagar
options.C: Hassan
options.D: Uttara Kannada

questions.explanation: Hassan was listed as Zone II only in the 2022 MoES table. Mysuru, Chamarajanagar and Uttara Kannada contain Zone III areas (often alongside Zone II portions).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as Zone II only in the 2022 MoES table for Karnataka?

options.A: Mandya
options.B: Bengaluru Rural
options.C: Tumakuru
options.D: Belagavi

questions.explanation: Belagavi contains Zone III areas (alongside Zone II portions) in the 2022 MoES table. Mandya, Bengaluru Rural and Tumakuru were listed as Zone II only.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the epicentre is correct?

options.A: The epicentre is always deeper than the focus
options.B: The epicentre is the point on the Earth's surface vertically above the focus
options.C: The epicentre is the same as the hypocentre
options.D: The epicentre is always the place of maximum damage

questions.explanation: The epicentre is the point on the Earth's surface vertically above the earthquake focus. The focus (hypocentre) is inside the Earth. The epicentre is not always the place of maximum damage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the focus is correct?

options.A: The focus is on the Earth's surface
options.B: The focus is also called the hypocentre and is the point inside the Earth where rupture begins
options.C: The focus is always shallower than 10 km
options.D: The focus is the same as the epicentre

questions.explanation: The focus, also called the hypocentre, is the point inside the Earth where the rupture begins and seismic energy is first released.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about focal depth classification is correct?

options.A: Shallow-focus earthquakes occur at 0-70 km depth
options.B: Intermediate-focus earthquakes occur at 0-70 km depth
options.C: Deep-focus earthquakes occur at 70-300 km depth
options.D: Shallow-focus earthquakes occur at 300-700 km depth

questions.explanation: A common broad classification is shallow-focus earthquakes (0-70 km), intermediate-focus earthquakes (70-300 km) and deep-focus earthquakes (300-700 km). Boundaries are approximate and conventions may vary slightly.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about focal depth classification is correct?

options.A: Intermediate-focus earthquakes occur at 70-300 km depth
options.B: Deep-focus earthquakes occur at 0-70 km depth
options.C: Shallow-focus earthquakes occur at 70-300 km depth
options.D: Intermediate-focus earthquakes occur at 300-700 km depth

questions.explanation: A common broad classification is shallow-focus earthquakes (0-70 km), intermediate-focus earthquakes (70-300 km) and deep-focus earthquakes (300-700 km).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about focal depth classification is correct?

options.A: Deep-focus earthquakes occur at 300-700 km depth
options.B: Shallow-focus earthquakes occur at 300-700 km depth
options.C: Intermediate-focus earthquakes occur at 0-70 km depth
options.D: Deep-focus earthquakes occur at 0-70 km depth

questions.explanation: A common broad classification is shallow-focus earthquakes (0-70 km), intermediate-focus earthquakes (70-300 km) and deep-focus earthquakes (300-700 km).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the primary difference between a seismograph and a seismogram?

options.A: A seismograph is the recorded trace; a seismogram is the instrument
options.B: A seismograph is the instrument or recording system; a seismogram is the recorded trace or digital record of ground motion
options.C: They are the same thing
options.D: A seismograph measures magnitude; a seismogram measures intensity

questions.explanation: A seismograph is an instrument or recording system used to detect and record ground motion. A seismogram is the recorded trace or digital record of ground motion produced by a seismograph.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the primary difference between a seismograph and a seismometer?

options.A: A seismograph is the sensor; a seismometer is the complete instrument
options.B: In common usage, a seismograph may refer to the complete instrument and recording system, while a seismometer refers more specifically to the sensing component
options.C: They are unrelated instruments
options.D: A seismometer records ground motion; a seismograph predicts earthquakes

questions.explanation: A seismometer is the sensor that measures ground motion. In common usage, seismograph may refer to the complete instrument and recording system, while seismometer refers more specifically to the sensing component.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How many suitably placed stations are needed to estimate the epicentre using triangulation?

options.A: At least one
options.B: At least two
options.C: At least three
options.D: At least five

questions.explanation: The time difference between P-wave and S-wave arrivals is used to estimate the distance from a station to the earthquake. Data from at least three suitably placed stations can be used for triangulation to estimate the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which time difference is used to estimate the distance from a station to an earthquake?

options.A: The time difference between P-wave and surface wave arrivals
options.B: The time difference between P-wave and S-wave arrivals
options.C: The time difference between S-wave and surface wave arrivals
options.D: The time difference between Love wave and Rayleigh wave arrivals

questions.explanation: The time difference between P-wave and S-wave arrivals is used to estimate the distance from a station to the earthquake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which instrument is especially useful for engineering design and analysing the shaking experienced by structures?

options.A: Seismogram
options.B: Accelerograph
options.C: Seismometer
options.D: Magnetometer

questions.explanation: An accelerograph is an instrument that records ground acceleration, especially strong ground motion. It is useful for engineering design and analysing the shaking experienced by structures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale's basis?

options.A: Seismic recordings and calculations
options.B: Observed effects, reports and damage patterns
options.C: Seismic moment calculations
options.D: Satellite measurements

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale is determined using observed effects, reports and damage patterns. Magnitude scales are determined using seismic recordings and calculations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes magnitude's determination?

options.A: Observed effects, reports and damage patterns
options.B: Seismic recordings and calculations
options.C: Human observations only
options.D: Building damage surveys

questions.explanation: Magnitude is determined using seismic recordings and calculations. Intensity is determined using observed effects, reports and damage patterns.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common scale for measuring magnitude?

options.A: Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI)
options.B: MSK
options.C: Local/Richter magnitude (ML) and moment magnitude (Mw)
options.D: EMS

questions.explanation: Common scales for measuring magnitude include Local/Richter magnitude (ML) and moment magnitude (Mw). Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI), MSK and EMS are intensity scales.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a common scale for measuring intensity?

options.A: Moment magnitude (Mw)
options.B: Local/Richter magnitude (ML)
options.C: Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI), MSK, EMS
options.D: Seismic moment

questions.explanation: Common scales for measuring intensity include Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI), MSK and EMS. Moment magnitude and Richter magnitude are magnitude scales.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between magnitude and intensity values?

options.A: One earthquake has many principal magnitude estimates but one intensity value
options.B: One earthquake has one principal magnitude estimate but can have many intensity values across the affected region
options.C: Both magnitude and intensity are single values per earthquake
options.D: Both magnitude and intensity vary from place to place

questions.explanation: One earthquake has one principal magnitude estimate but can have many intensity values across the affected region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes seismic moment?

options.A: It is calculated from the rigidity of the rocks, the area of the fault rupture and the average displacement along the fault
options.B: It is based on observed damage patterns
options.C: It is based on recorded wave amplitudes only
options.D: It is a measure of tsunami height

questions.explanation: Seismic moment is a measure of the physical size of an earthquake source. It is calculated from the rigidity of the rocks, the area of the fault rupture and the average displacement along the fault.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Richter scale and energy?

options.A: A one-unit increase corresponds to ten times the energy release
options.B: The energy released increases by roughly 32 times for each whole-number magnitude step
options.C: A one-unit increase corresponds to two times the energy release
options.D: Energy release is not related to magnitude

questions.explanation: The energy released increases by roughly 32 times for each whole-number magnitude step as a useful approximation. A one-unit increase corresponds to ten times the recorded wave amplitude, not ten times energy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the development of the Richter scale?

options.A: Developed by Thomas C. Hanks and Hiroo Kanamori in 1979
options.B: Developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935 to quantify the size of relatively nearby earthquakes in southern California
options.C: Developed by Giuseppe Mercalli in 1902
options.D: Developed by the Bureau of Indian Standards

questions.explanation: The Richter scale is the common name for the local magnitude scale (ML), developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935 to quantify the size of relatively nearby earthquakes in southern California using recorded seismic-wave amplitudes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the development of the moment magnitude scale?

options.A: Developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935
options.B: Introduced by Thomas C. Hanks and Hiroo Kanamori in 1979
options.C: Developed by Giuseppe Mercalli
options.D: Developed by the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services

questions.explanation: Thomas C. Hanks and Hiroo Kanamori introduced the moment magnitude scale in 1979.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale's range?

options.A: 10 levels, from I to X
options.B: 12 levels, from I to XII
options.C: 8 levels, from I to VIII
options.D: 15 levels, from I to XV

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale has 12 levels, from I (not felt or felt by very few) to XII (total or near-total destruction in the traditional description).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the approximate distribution of India's land area among seismic zones?

options.A: About 5% in Zone V, 10% in Zone IV, 20% in Zone III, and the rest in Zone II
options.B: About 11% in Zone V, 18% in Zone IV, 30% in Zone III and the remaining area in Zone II
options.C: About 25% in Zone V, 25% in Zone IV, 25% in Zone III, and 25% in Zone II
options.D: About 50% in Zone V and 50% in Zone IV

questions.explanation: A Ministry of Earth Sciences parliamentary answer in 2022 gave approximate figures of about 11% in Zone V, 18% in Zone IV, 30% in Zone III and the remaining area in Zone II.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a human-induced cause of earthquakes?

options.A: Plate tectonic movement
options.B: Magma movement
options.C: Reservoir impoundment
options.D: Meteorite impact

questions.explanation: Human-induced or induced seismicity can result from activities such as reservoir impoundment, mining, fluid injection or extraction, and some underground engineering operations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an induced earthquake?

options.A: An earthquake caused by sudden slip along a fault due to tectonic stress
options.B: An earthquake caused by magma movement
options.C: An earthquake associated with deep fluid injection
options.D: An earthquake caused by underground mine collapse

questions.explanation: Induced earthquakes can result from activities such as reservoir impoundment, mining, fluid injection or extraction, and some underground engineering operations. An earthquake associated with deep fluid injection is an example of induced seismicity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a collapse earthquake?

options.A: An earthquake caused by sudden slip along a fault due to tectonic stress
options.B: An earthquake caused by magma movement
options.C: An earthquake that may occur when underground cavities or mines collapse
options.D: An earthquake caused by reservoir impoundment

questions.explanation: Collapse earthquakes may occur when underground cavities or mines collapse.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a volcanic earthquake?

options.A: An earthquake caused by sudden slip along a fault due to tectonic stress
options.B: An earthquake associated with magma movement, fracturing of rocks and pressure changes in a volcanic system
options.C: An earthquake caused by underground mine collapse
options.D: An earthquake caused by reservoir impoundment

questions.explanation: A volcanic earthquake is seismic activity associated with magma movement, fracturing of rocks and pressure changes in a volcanic system. It may occur before or during an eruption, but not every volcanic earthquake leads to an eruption.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a tectonic earthquake?

options.A: An earthquake caused by sudden movement along a fault due to tectonic stress
options.B: An earthquake caused by magma movement
options.C: An earthquake caused by underground mine collapse
options.D: An earthquake caused by reservoir impoundment

questions.explanation: A tectonic earthquake is caused by sudden movement along a fault due to tectonic stress. Such earthquakes are especially common near plate boundaries but can also occur within plates along older or reactivated faults.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about shallow earthquakes is correct?

options.A: They always cause more damage than deep earthquakes
options.B: When other factors are similar, a shallow earthquake generally releases energy closer to the surface, so strong shaking may occur near the source
options.C: They occur at depths greater than 300 km
options.D: They are always less damaging than deep earthquakes

questions.explanation: When other factors are similar, a shallow earthquake generally releases energy closer to the surface, so strong shaking may occur near the source. Actual damage still depends on magnitude, geology, buildings and distance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake damage and the epicentre is correct?

options.A: The epicentre is always the place of maximum damage
options.B: The epicentre is never the place of maximum damage
options.C: The epicentre may be near the area of strongest shaking, but not necessarily; local soil amplification, rupture direction, depth, building vulnerability and other factors can cause maximum damage away from the epicentre
options.D: Maximum damage always occurs exactly at the epicentre

questions.explanation: The epicentre may be near the area of strongest shaking, but not necessarily. Local soil amplification, rupture direction, depth, building vulnerability and other factors can cause maximum damage away from the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale is correct?

options.A: It measures the total energy released at the focus
options.B: It is a single value for an earthquake event
options.C: It describes the observed effects and shaking at a location, not the total energy released at the earthquake source
options.D: It is a logarithmic magnitude scale

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale describes the observed effects and shaking at a location, not the total energy released at the earthquake source. It can vary from place to place for the same earthquake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the moment magnitude scale is correct?

options.A: It is based on observed damage patterns
options.B: It is based on seismic moment and is preferred for large earthquakes
options.C: It has 12 levels, from I to XII
options.D: It saturates for very large earthquakes

questions.explanation: Moment magnitude (Mw) is a logarithmic magnitude scale based on seismic moment. It is preferred for large earthquakes because it does not saturate in the same way as older magnitude scales for very large events.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic zoning in India is correct?

options.A: India has five seismic zones: I, II, III, IV and V
options.B: India's commonly cited BIS framework classifies India into four zones: II, III, IV and V; Zone V is the highest and Zone II is the lowest
options.C: Zone I is the highest seismic-hazard zone
options.D: Seismic zoning predicts the exact date of earthquakes

questions.explanation: The BIS seismic zoning framework in IS 1893 (Part 1): 2016 classifies India into four zones: Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV and Zone V. Zone V is the highest seismic-hazard zone and Zone II is the lowest in the four-zone scheme.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Karnataka's seismic zones is correct?

options.A: Karnataka is entirely in Zone V
options.B: Karnataka includes Zone II and Zone III areas; there are no Zone IV or Zone V areas in the official district-wise summary cited by the Ministry of Earth Sciences
options.C: Karnataka is entirely in Zone IV
options.D: Karnataka has no seismic monitoring

questions.explanation: Karnataka includes areas classified in Seismic Zone II and Zone III under the BIS seismic zoning map. There are no Zone IV or Zone V areas in the official district-wise summary cited by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami warning is correct?

options.A: People should wait for an official warning after a strong coastal earthquake before evacuating
options.B: If a person is in a coastal area and experiences strong or prolonged earthquake shaking, they should move immediately to higher ground or inland when safe to do so; do not wait for an official alert
options.C: A tsunami warning means the danger is over after the first wave
options.D: INCOIS operates Karnataka's seismic monitoring network
