questions.explanation: If a person is in a coastal area and experiences strong or prolonged earthquake shaking, they should move immediately to higher ground or inland when safe to do so. Do not wait for an official alert.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake preparedness is correct?

options.A: During indoor shaking, you should run outside immediately
options.B: During indoor shaking, you should Drop, Cover and Hold On; do not run outside while the building is shaking
options.C: You should use elevators during an earthquake to evacuate quickly
options.D: You should store heavy objects above beds

questions.explanation: During indoor shaking, you should Drop, Cover and Hold On. Do not run outside while the building is shaking. Do not use elevators during shaking or immediately after an earthquake. Keep heavy objects on lower shelves, not above beds.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake early-warning systems is correct?

options.A: They provide long-term prediction of the exact date, location and magnitude of future earthquakes
options.B: They detect faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source and send alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives; they provide seconds to tens of seconds in some situations
options.C: They prevent earthquakes from occurring
options.D: They are operated by KSNDMC in Karnataka

questions.explanation: An earthquake early-warning system detects the faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source and sends alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives. It provides seconds to tens of seconds in some situations, not long-term prediction, and may not provide warning close to the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake-resistant construction is correct?

options.A: It guarantees that buildings will never suffer any damage
options.B: It aims to improve structural strength, ductility, connections and overall performance to resist expected earthquake forces without unacceptable collapse or loss of life
options.C: Ductility means the ability of a material to conduct electricity
options.D: Retrofitting is the construction of new buildings

questions.explanation: Earthquake-resistant construction is the design and construction of buildings and infrastructure to resist expected earthquake forces without unacceptable collapse or loss of life. It aims to improve structural strength, ductility, connections and overall performance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about retrofitting is correct?

options.A: Retrofitting is the demolition of old buildings
options.B: Retrofitting is the strengthening or modification of an existing building or structure to improve its resistance to earthquake shaking
options.C: Retrofitting is the construction of new buildings
options.D: Retrofitting is the process of predicting earthquakes

questions.explanation: Retrofitting is the strengthening or modification of an existing building or structure to improve its resistance to earthquake shaking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake prediction is correct?

options.A: Scientists can reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake
options.B: Scientists can estimate seismic hazard and probabilities over time, monitor earthquakes and issue alerts after an earthquake has begun, but they cannot reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake
options.C: Earthquake early-warning systems provide long-term prediction
options.D: All earthquakes can be predicted weeks in advance

questions.explanation: Scientists can estimate seismic hazard and probabilities over time, monitor earthquakes and issue alerts after an earthquake has begun, but they cannot reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the effects of tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Tsunamis only affect the immediate coastline and cannot cause damage far inland
options.B: Tsunamis can cause coastal flooding and inundation, strong currents, drowning, injuries and deaths, destruction of buildings and infrastructure, erosion, saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater, damage to ports and fisheries, displacement of communities and economic disruption
options.C: Tsunamis have no effect on agriculture
options.D: Tsunamis improve soil fertility

questions.explanation: Major effects of tsunamis include coastal flooding and inundation, strong currents, drowning, injuries and deaths, destruction of buildings and infrastructure, erosion, saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater, damage to ports and fisheries, displacement of communities and economic disruption.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami is correct?

options.A: It was generated by a volcanic eruption in Indonesia
options.B: It was generated by the great undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004 and affected many countries around the Indian Ocean, including India's east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
options.C: It affected only the west coast of India
options.D: It was caused by a meteorite impact

questions.explanation: The 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami was a devastating tsunami generated by the great undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004. It affected many countries around the Indian Ocean, including India's east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the west coast of India and tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Only the east coast of India can experience tsunamis
options.B: Although exposure differs from the east coast, the west coast is not immune to tsunami hazards; tsunami risk depends on the location and characteristics of the generating event and the propagation path
options.C: The west coast has never experienced a tsunami
options.D: The west coast is protected by the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: Although exposure differs from the east coast, the west coast is not immune to tsunami hazards. Tsunami risk depends on the location and characteristics of the generating event and the propagation path.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami run-up and inundation is correct?

options.A: Run-up and inundation mean the same thing
options.B: Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land; inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline
options.C: Run-up is the horizontal penetration of water inland; inundation is the maximum vertical height
options.D: Both run-up and inundation measure tsunami speed

questions.explanation: Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land. Inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami causes is correct?

options.A: All undersea earthquakes generate tsunamis
options.B: Large, shallow undersea earthquakes that cause significant vertical displacement of the seabed are the most common cause of major destructive tsunamis; submarine landslides and volcanic activity can also generate tsunamis
options.C: Tsunamis are caused only by meteorite impacts
options.D: Tsunamis are caused by daily tides

questions.explanation: Large, shallow undersea earthquakes that cause significant vertical displacement of the seabed are the most common cause of major destructive tsunamis. Submarine landslides and volcanic activity can also generate tsunamis. Not all undersea earthquakes generate tsunamis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the difference between a tsunami and an ordinary sea wave is correct?

options.A: They are identical
options.B: Ordinary wind-generated waves mainly affect the ocean surface and have much shorter wavelengths; a tsunami involves the movement of a large water column, has a very long wavelength and period, and can travel across ocean basins
options.C: A tsunami has a shorter wavelength than an ordinary wave
options.D: Ordinary waves can travel across ocean basins faster than tsunamis

questions.explanation: Ordinary wind-generated waves mainly affect the ocean surface and have much shorter wavelengths. A tsunami involves the movement of a large water column, has a very long wavelength and period, and can travel across ocean basins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about tsunami waves in deep ocean water is correct?

options.A: Tsunami waves have very high wave height in deep water
options.B: In deep water, tsunami waves may have low wave height but very long wavelengths and travel at high speeds; their height increases as they enter shallow coastal waters and slow down
options.C: Tsunami waves travel slowly in deep water
options.D: Tsunami waves are easily noticed by ships in deep water

questions.explanation: In deep water, tsunami waves may have low wave height but very long wavelengths and travel at high speeds. Their height increases as they enter shallow coastal waters and slow down.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the first tsunami wave is correct?

options.A: The first wave is always the largest
options.B: The first wave may not be the largest, and dangerous currents can continue for hours; a tsunami is usually a series of waves
options.C: The first wave is always the smallest
options.D: A tsunami is a single wave

questions.explanation: A tsunami is usually a series of waves. The first wave may not be the largest, and dangerous currents can continue for hours.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the word 'tsunami' is correct?

options.A: It is a Chinese word meaning 'great wave'
options.B: It is Japanese: tsu means harbour and nami means wave
options.C: It is a Sanskrit word meaning 'ocean surge'
options.D: It is a Greek word meaning 'sea motion'

questions.explanation: The word tsunami is Japanese: tsu means harbour and nami means wave.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic waves and recording is correct?

options.A: Seismic waves are sound waves
options.B: Seismic waves are waves of energy generated by an earthquake or other source and transmitted through the Earth or along its surface; they are recorded by seismological instruments
options.C: Seismic waves are electromagnetic waves
options.D: Seismic waves cannot be recorded

questions.explanation: Seismic waves are waves of energy generated by an earthquake or other source and transmitted through the Earth or along its surface. They are recorded by seismological instruments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the two broad groups of seismic waves is correct?

options.A: Body waves travel along the surface; surface waves travel through Earth's interior
options.B: Body waves travel through Earth's interior; surface waves travel along or near Earth's surface
options.C: Both body and surface waves travel only through the interior
options.D: Both body and surface waves travel only along the surface

questions.explanation: Body waves travel through Earth's interior; surface waves travel along or near Earth's surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about surface waves is correct?

options.A: Surface waves are generally faster than body waves
options.B: Surface waves are generally slower than body waves but can produce large-amplitude shaking and substantial damage
options.C: Surface waves travel through the Earth's core
options.D: Surface waves cannot cause damage

questions.explanation: Surface waves travel along the Earth's surface or near-surface layers. They are generally slower than body waves but can produce large-amplitude shaking and substantial damage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about P-waves is correct?

options.A: P-waves are shear waves that cannot travel through liquids
options.B: P-waves are primary or compressional seismic waves; they are the fastest seismic body waves and are generally recorded first by a seismograph
options.C: P-waves are surface waves
options.D: P-waves arrive after S-waves

questions.explanation: P-waves are primary or compressional seismic waves. They are the fastest seismic body waves and are generally recorded first by a seismograph.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about S-waves is correct?

options.A: S-waves are primary waves that travel through all mediums
options.B: S-waves are secondary or shear seismic waves; they are slower than P-waves and generally arrive second at a recording station
options.C: S-waves are surface waves
options.D: S-waves arrive before P-waves

questions.explanation: S-waves are secondary or shear seismic waves. They are slower than P-waves and generally arrive second at a recording station.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Love waves is correct?

options.A: Love waves produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion similar to ocean waves
options.B: Love waves produce mainly horizontal side-to-side shear motion, generally perpendicular to the direction of propagation, without the vertical rolling motion characteristic of Rayleigh waves
options.C: Love waves are body waves
options.D: Love waves are compressional waves

questions.explanation: Love waves produce mainly horizontal side-to-side shear motion, generally perpendicular to the direction of propagation, without the vertical rolling motion characteristic of Rayleigh waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Rayleigh waves is correct?

options.A: Rayleigh waves produce only horizontal side-to-side motion
options.B: Rayleigh waves produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion that includes both vertical and horizontal components, similar in broad appearance to ocean waves
options.C: Rayleigh waves are body waves
options.D: Rayleigh waves are compressional waves

questions.explanation: Rayleigh waves produce a rolling, elliptical particle motion that includes both vertical and horizontal components, similar in broad appearance to ocean waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why S-waves cannot travel through liquids is correct?

options.A: Liquids are too dense for S-waves
options.B: Liquids do not support the shear rigidity required for shear waves
options.C: S-waves are too fast for liquids
options.D: Liquids absorb all seismic waves

questions.explanation: S-waves cannot propagate through liquids because liquids do not support the shear rigidity required for shear waves. Their absence through Earth's liquid outer core is important evidence that the outer core is liquid.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the importance of S-waves in understanding Earth's interior is correct?

options.A: S-waves travel through the core, proving it is solid
options.B: Their inability to travel through liquids helps scientists infer the liquid state of the outer core; changes in seismic-wave speeds and paths also reveal internal boundaries and material properties
options.C: S-waves are the fastest waves and reveal the crust's thickness
options.D: S-waves cannot provide any information about Earth's interior

questions.explanation: Their inability to travel through liquids helps scientists infer the liquid state of the outer core. Changes in seismic-wave speeds and paths also reveal internal boundaries and material properties.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why surface waves can be highly destructive is correct?

options.A: They travel through the Earth's core
options.B: They often have large amplitudes and can produce prolonged horizontal and vertical ground motion near the surface, which may strongly affect buildings, bridges and other structures
options.C: They are the fastest seismic waves
options.D: They only occur in coastal areas

questions.explanation: Surface waves often have large amplitudes and can produce prolonged horizontal and vertical ground motion near the surface, which may strongly affect buildings, bridges and other structures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how earthquakes are located using seismograms is correct?

options.A: By measuring surface waves only
options.B: The time difference between P-wave and S-wave arrivals is used to estimate the distance from a station to the earthquake; data from at least three suitably placed stations can be used for triangulation to estimate the epicentre
options.C: By measuring temperature at the epicentre
options.D: By using satellite images only

questions.explanation: The time difference between P-wave and S-wave arrivals is used to estimate the distance from a station to the earthquake. Data from at least three suitably placed stations can be used for triangulation to estimate the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a seismograph can measure earthquake magnitude directly is correct?

options.A: A seismograph directly measures magnitude without calculations
options.B: A seismograph records ground motion; magnitude is calculated from recorded wave amplitudes and other parameters, with corrections for distance, frequency, instrument response and, depending on the scale, seismic moment
options.C: Seismographs cannot record ground motion
options.D: Only digital seismographs can measure magnitude

questions.explanation: A seismograph records ground motion. Magnitude is calculated from recorded wave amplitudes and other parameters, with corrections for distance, frequency, instrument response and, depending on the scale, seismic moment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about an accelerograph is correct?

options.A: It measures tsunami height
options.B: It records ground acceleration, especially strong ground motion, and is useful for engineering design and analysing the shaking experienced by structures
options.C: It predicts earthquakes
options.D: It measures the depth of an earthquake

questions.explanation: An accelerograph is an instrument that records ground acceleration, especially strong ground motion. It is useful for engineering design and analysing the shaking experienced by structures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake magnitude is correct?

options.A: Magnitude describes the local effects of shaking at a site
options.B: Magnitude is a quantitative measure of the size of an earthquake at its source, expressed as a single value for an event, although different magnitude scales may produce slightly different values
options.C: Magnitude varies from place to place for the same earthquake
options.D: Magnitude is measured using observed damage patterns

questions.explanation: Magnitude is a quantitative measure of the size of an earthquake at its source. It is expressed as a single value for an event, although different magnitude scales may produce slightly different values.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about earthquake intensity is correct?

options.A: Intensity estimates the size of the earthquake source
options.B: Intensity describes the observed strength of shaking and its effects at a particular location, including how people feel it and the damage to buildings and the environment; it can vary from place to place for the same earthquake
options.C: Intensity is a single value for an earthquake event
options.D: Intensity is measured using seismic recordings only

questions.explanation: Intensity describes the observed strength of shaking and its effects at a particular location, including how people feel it and the damage to buildings and the environment. It can vary from place to place for the same earthquake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the difference between magnitude and intensity is correct?

options.A: Magnitude describes local effects; intensity estimates the size of the earthquake source
options.B: Magnitude estimates the size of the earthquake source; intensity describes the local effects of shaking at a site; one earthquake has one principal magnitude estimate but can have many intensity values across the affected region
options.C: Both measure the same thing
options.D: Magnitude varies from place to place; intensity is a single value

questions.explanation: Magnitude estimates the size of the earthquake source; intensity describes the local effects of shaking at a site. One earthquake has one principal magnitude estimate but can have many intensity values across the affected region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Richter scale is correct?

options.A: It is a linear scale
options.B: It is the common name for the local magnitude scale (ML), developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935 to quantify the size of relatively nearby earthquakes in southern California using recorded seismic-wave amplitudes
options.C: It is based on seismic moment
options.D: It measures observed shaking and damage

questions.explanation: The Richter scale is the common name for the local magnitude scale (ML), developed by Charles F. Richter in 1935 to quantify the size of relatively nearby earthquakes in southern California using recorded seismic-wave amplitudes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether the Richter scale is linear is correct?

options.A: It is linear
options.B: It is logarithmic; a one-unit increase corresponds to ten times the recorded wave amplitude under the scale's defined conditions, and the energy released increases by roughly 32 times for each whole-number magnitude step
options.C: It is logarithmic but a one-unit increase means two times amplitude
options.D: It is linear for small earthquakes only

questions.explanation: The Richter scale is logarithmic. A one-unit increase corresponds to ten times the recorded wave amplitude under the scale's defined conditions. The energy released increases by roughly 32 times for each whole-number magnitude step as a useful approximation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether the Richter scale is suitable for all very large earthquakes is correct?

options.A: It works for all earthquake sizes
options.B: The original local magnitude scale can saturate for large earthquakes and is not ideal for very large or distant events; modern reporting generally favours moment magnitude for large earthquakes
options.C: It works only for deep earthquakes
options.D: It works only for volcanic earthquakes

questions.explanation: The original local magnitude scale can saturate for large earthquakes and is not ideal for very large or distant events. Modern reporting generally favours moment magnitude for large earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the energy release of a magnitude 6 versus magnitude 5 earthquake is correct?

options.A: A magnitude 6 earthquake releases ten times the energy of a magnitude 5 earthquake
options.B: The recorded wave amplitude is about ten times greater for a one-unit increase, while the energy release is approximately 32 times greater
options.C: Both amplitude and energy increase ten times per unit
options.D: Energy increases only two times per unit

questions.explanation: The recorded wave amplitude is about ten times greater for a one-unit increase, while the energy release is approximately 32 times greater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the moment magnitude scale is correct?

options.A: It measures observed shaking and damage at a location
options.B: It is a logarithmic magnitude scale based on seismic moment, which reflects the rigidity of rocks, the area of the fault that slipped and the average amount of slip
options.C: It was developed by Charles Richter in 1935
options.D: It measures tsunami run-up

questions.explanation: Moment magnitude (Mw) is a logarithmic magnitude scale based on seismic moment, which reflects the rigidity of rocks, the area of the fault that slipped and the average amount of slip.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why moment magnitude is preferred for large earthquakes is correct?

options.A: It is easier to calculate than the Richter scale
options.B: It is physically related to the size of the earthquake source and does not saturate in the same way as older magnitude scales for very large events; it provides a consistent measure across a wide range of earthquake sizes
options.C: It measures intensity directly
options.D: It was developed before the Richter scale

questions.explanation: Moment magnitude is physically related to the size of the earthquake source and does not saturate in the same way as older magnitude scales for very large events. It provides a consistent measure across a wide range of earthquake sizes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic moment is correct?

options.A: It is the observed damage at a location
options.B: It is a measure of the physical size of an earthquake source, calculated from the rigidity of the rocks, the area of the fault rupture and the average displacement along the fault
options.C: It is the time difference between P-wave and S-wave arrivals
options.D: It is the depth of the earthquake focus

questions.explanation: Seismic moment is a measure of the physical size of an earthquake source. It is calculated from the rigidity of the rocks, the area of the fault rupture and the average displacement along the fault.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about who developed the moment magnitude scale is correct?

options.A: Charles F. Richter
options.B: Thomas C. Hanks and Hiroo Kanamori introduced the moment magnitude scale in 1979
options.C: Giuseppe Mercalli
options.D: John Milne

questions.explanation: Thomas C. Hanks and Hiroo Kanamori introduced the moment magnitude scale in 1979.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mercalli intensity scale is correct?

options.A: It is based on seismic moment
options.B: The Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale describes the effects of earthquake shaking at a particular location, based on human observations, effects on objects, and damage to structures
options.C: It measures the size of the earthquake source
options.D: It measures tsunami wave height

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity (MMI) scale describes the effects of earthquake shaking at a particular location, based on human observations, effects on objects, and damage to structures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the number of levels in the Modified Mercalli Intensity scale is correct?

options.A: 10 levels, from I to X
options.B: 12 levels, from I to XII
options.C: 8 levels, from I to VIII
options.D: 15 levels, from I to XV

questions.explanation: The Modified Mercalli Intensity scale has 12 levels, from I (not felt or felt by very few) to XII (total or near-total destruction in the traditional description).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether Mercalli intensity measures energy released at the focus is correct?

options.A: It measures the total energy released
options.B: It describes the observed effects and shaking at a location, not the total energy released at the earthquake source
options.C: It measures energy only for shallow earthquakes
options.D: It measures both energy and effects

questions.explanation: The Mercalli intensity scale describes the observed effects and shaking at a location, not the total energy released at the earthquake source.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why the same earthquake can have different Mercalli intensities is correct?

options.A: Because the magnitude changes from place to place
options.B: Shaking varies with distance from the source, depth, local geology, soil conditions, topography and building vulnerability, so intensity differs across locations
options.C: Because the focus moves during the earthquake
options.D: Because the scale is not standardized

questions.explanation: Shaking varies with distance from the source, depth, local geology, soil conditions, topography and building vulnerability. Therefore, intensity differs across locations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI level I is correct?

options.A: Total destruction
options.B: Not felt except by very few under especially favourable conditions
options.C: Severe shaking with considerable damage
options.D: Moderate shaking felt by all

questions.explanation: MMI level I indicates not felt except by very few under especially favourable conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI level XII is correct?

options.A: Not felt
options.B: Weak shaking felt by some people
options.C: Total or near-total destruction in the traditional description
options.D: Light shaking with no damage

questions.explanation: MMI level XII indicates total or near-total destruction in the traditional description.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI levels II-III is correct?

options.A: Extreme to catastrophic effects
options.B: Weak shaking; felt by some people, especially indoors
options.C: Severe to violent shaking
options.D: Total destruction

questions.explanation: MMI levels II-III indicate weak shaking; felt by some people, especially indoors.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI levels IV-V is correct?

options.A: Not felt
options.B: Light to moderate shaking; noticeable movement of objects
options.C: Total destruction
options.D: Extreme damage

questions.explanation: MMI levels IV-V indicate light to moderate shaking; noticeable movement of objects.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI levels VI-VII is correct?

options.A: Weak shaking felt indoors
options.B: Strong to very strong shaking; slight to moderate damage may occur
options.C: Extreme to catastrophic effects
options.D: Not felt at all

questions.explanation: MMI levels VI-VII indicate strong to very strong shaking; slight to moderate damage may occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI levels VIII-IX is correct?

options.A: Light shaking
options.B: Severe to violent shaking; considerable damage in vulnerable structures
options.C: No damage
options.D: Weak shaking felt by few

questions.explanation: MMI levels VIII-IX indicate severe to violent shaking; considerable damage in vulnerable structures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about MMI levels X-XII is correct?

options.A: Weak shaking
options.B: Extreme to catastrophic effects; very severe damage and major changes to the built or natural environment
options.C: Light to moderate shaking
options.D: Moderate damage only

questions.explanation: MMI levels X-XII indicate extreme to catastrophic effects; very severe damage and major changes to the built or natural environment.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about seismic zoning is correct?

options.A: It predicts the exact date of earthquakes
options.B: Seismic zoning divides a region into areas according to expected levels of earthquake ground shaking or seismic hazard for planning and engineering purposes; it helps guide earthquake-resistant construction and risk reduction
options.C: It measures the magnitude of earthquakes
options.D: It is the study of seismic waves

questions.explanation: Seismic zoning divides a region into areas according to expected levels of earthquake ground shaking or seismic hazard for planning and engineering purposes. It helps guide earthquake-resistant construction and risk reduction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the number of seismic zones in India's current commonly cited BIS zoning framework is correct?

options.A: Three zones: II, III, IV
options.B: Four zones: II, III, IV and V; Zone I is not used in this current four-zone classification
options.C: Five zones: I, II, III, IV, V
options.D: Six zones

questions.explanation: The BIS seismic zoning framework in IS 1893 (Part 1): 2016 classifies India into four zones: Zone II, Zone III, Zone IV and Zone V. Zone I is not used in this current four-zone classification.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the most earthquake-prone seismic zone in India's four-zone classification is correct?

options.A: Zone II
options.B: Zone III
options.C: Zone IV
options.D: Zone V is the highest seismic-hazard zone in the four-zone classification

questions.explanation: Zone V is the highest seismic-hazard zone in the four-zone classification.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the least severe seismic zone in India's four-zone classification is correct?

options.A: Zone II is the lowest seismic-hazard zone in the four-zone classification; it does not mean that earthquakes are impossible there
options.B: Zone III
options.C: Zone IV
options.D: Zone V

questions.explanation: Zone II is the lowest seismic-hazard zone in the four-zone classification; it does not mean that earthquakes are impossible there.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the parts of India broadly associated with Zone V is correct?

options.A: Only the Deccan Plateau
options.B: Much of the northeastern region, parts of the Himalayan belt, the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat, parts of northern Bihar and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
options.C: Only coastal Kerala
options.D: Only Rajasthan

questions.explanation: The highest-hazard areas include much of the northeastern region, parts of the Himalayan belt, the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat, parts of northern Bihar and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Exact boundaries should be checked on the applicable BIS seismic zoning map.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the areas broadly associated with Zone IV is correct?

options.A: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands only
options.B: Parts of the Himalayan and sub-Himalayan region, Delhi and other selected areas
options.C: Only the Rann of Kutch
options.D: Only peninsular India

questions.explanation: Parts of the Himalayan and sub-Himalayan region, Delhi and other selected areas fall in Zone IV. The exact pattern is map-specific and should be read from the official BIS map rather than inferred from state boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the approximate distribution of India's land area among seismic zones is correct?

options.A: About 5% in Zone V, 10% in Zone IV, 20% in Zone III, and the rest in Zone II
options.B: About 11% in Zone V, 18% in Zone IV, 30% in Zone III and the remaining area in Zone II
options.C: About 25% in Zone V, 25% in Zone IV, 25% in Zone III, and 25% in Zone II
options.D: About 50% in Zone V and 50% in Zone IV

questions.explanation: A Ministry of Earth Sciences parliamentary answer in 2022 gave approximate figures of about 11% in Zone V, 18% in Zone IV, 30% in Zone III and the remaining area in Zone II. These are approximate area shares, not predictions of the probability of an earthquake in a particular year.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a seismic zone tells the exact probability or date of an earthquake is correct?

options.A: It predicts exactly when an earthquake will occur
options.B: Seismic zoning is a planning classification of expected hazard, not a prediction of when or exactly where an earthquake will occur
options.C: It gives the exact probability for each year
options.D: It predicts the magnitude but not the date

questions.explanation: Seismic zoning is a planning classification of expected hazard, not a prediction of when or exactly where an earthquake will occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether every location within one seismic zone experiences identical shaking is correct?

options.A: All locations in a zone experience identical shaking
options.B: Local soil, sediment thickness, topography, basin effects, fault proximity and building conditions can produce different levels of shaking within the same zone
options.C: Only locations in Zone V experience different shaking
options.D: Only locations in Zone II experience different shaking

questions.explanation: Local soil, sediment thickness, topography, basin effects, fault proximity and building conditions can produce different levels of shaking within the same zone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the seismic zones covering Karnataka is correct?

options.A: Zone IV and Zone V
options.B: Zone II and Zone III; there are no Zone IV or Zone V areas in the official district-wise summary cited by the Ministry of Earth Sciences
options.C: Zone I and Zone II
options.D: Zone V only

questions.explanation: Karnataka includes areas classified in Seismic Zone II and Zone III under the BIS seismic zoning map. There are no Zone IV or Zone V areas in the official district-wise summary cited by the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Karnataka districts listed as having Zone III areas in the Ministry of Earth Sciences' 2022 parliamentary answer is correct?

options.A: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Raichur, Koppal
options.B: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Uttara Kannada, Shivamogga, Udupi, Chikkamagaluru, Bengaluru, Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, Mysuru and Chamarajanagar
options.C: Gadag, Dharwad, Haveri, Ballari
options.D: Chitradurga, Davanagere, Tumakuru, Kolar

questions.explanation: The answer lists Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Uttara Kannada, Shivamogga, Udupi, Chikkamagaluru, Bengaluru (then listed as Bangalore), Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, Mysuru and Chamarajanagar as containing Zone III areas, often alongside Zone II portions. Udupi is listed as Zone III.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the districts listed as Zone II only in the 2022 MoES table is correct?

options.A: Belagavi, Bagalkot, Vijayapura, Uttara Kannada
options.B: Kalaburagi, Bidar, Raichur, Koppal, Gadag, Dharwad, Haveri, Ballari, Chitradurga, Davanagere, Tumakuru, Kolar, Bengaluru Rural, Mandya and Hassan
options.C: Shivamogga, Udupi, Chikkamagaluru, Bengaluru
options.D: Dakshina Kannada, Kodagu, Mysuru, Chamarajanagar

questions.explanation: Kalaburagi (then Gulbarga), Bidar, Raichur, Koppal, Gadag, Dharwad, Haveri, Ballari (then Bellary), Chitradurga, Davanagere, Tumakuru (then Tumkur), Kolar, Bengaluru Rural, Mandya and Hassan were listed as Zone II in that table.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the parts of Karnataka that deserve particular attention in earthquake risk planning is correct?

options.A: Only the eastern districts
options.B: The 2022 MoES table identifies Zone III portions in several districts, including parts of northern Karnataka, the western coastal belt and the southern/western districts
options.C: Only Bengaluru
options.D: Only the northern districts

questions.explanation: The 2022 MoES table identifies Zone III portions in several districts, including parts of northern Karnataka, the western coastal belt and the southern/western districts. Local hazard also depends on geology, site conditions and the vulnerability of buildings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the role of KSNDMC in Karnataka is correct?

options.A: It conducts elections in Karnataka
options.B: It is the Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre, the state's nodal agency for monitoring seismic activity with a network of permanent seismic monitoring stations across Karnataka
options.C: It builds earthquake-resistant buildings
options.D: It issues tsunami warnings for India

questions.explanation: The Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) is the state's nodal agency for monitoring seismic activity. Its published geological-hazard information describes a network of permanent seismic monitoring stations across Karnataka.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a lower seismic zone means Karnataka is earthquake-free is correct?

options.A: Zone II means no earthquakes can occur
options.B: Earthquakes can occur in Zone II as well as Zone III; the classification indicates relative design hazard, not zero risk
options.C: Only Zone III can experience earthquakes
options.D: Karnataka has never experienced an earthquake

questions.explanation: Earthquakes can occur in Zone II as well as Zone III. The classification indicates relative design hazard, not zero risk.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what a tsunami is is correct?

options.A: An ordinary wind-generated ocean wave
options.B: A series of long-period ocean waves generated by the sudden displacement of a large volume of water, which may travel across an ocean basin and produce severe coastal inundation when it reaches shallow water
options.C: A type of seismic wave that travels through the Earth
options.D: A tidal wave caused by the moon's gravity

questions.explanation: A tsunami is a series of long-period ocean waves generated by the sudden displacement of a large volume of water. It may travel across an ocean basin and produce severe coastal inundation when it reaches shallow water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the meaning of the word tsunami is correct?

options.A: It is a Chinese word meaning 'great wave'
options.B: It is Japanese: tsu means harbour and nami means wave
options.C: It is a Sanskrit word meaning 'ocean surge'
options.D: It is a Greek word meaning 'sea motion'

questions.explanation: The word is Japanese: tsu means harbour and nami means wave.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a tsunami is the same as an ordinary sea wave is correct?

options.A: They are identical
options.B: Ordinary wind-generated waves mainly affect the ocean surface and have much shorter wavelengths; a tsunami involves the movement of a large water column, has a very long wavelength and period, and can travel across ocean basins
options.C: Tsunamis are larger ordinary waves
options.D: Tsunamis are caused by wind

questions.explanation: Ordinary wind-generated waves mainly affect the ocean surface and have much shorter wavelengths. A tsunami involves the movement of a large water column, has a very long wavelength and period, and can travel across ocean basins.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a tsunami can consist of more than one wave is correct?

options.A: A tsunami is a single wave
options.B: A tsunami is usually a series of waves; the first wave may not be the largest, and dangerous currents can continue for hours
options.C: Only in the Pacific Ocean does a tsunami consist of multiple waves
options.D: Only volcanic tsunamis consist of multiple waves

questions.explanation: A tsunami is usually a series of waves. The first wave may not be the largest, and dangerous currents can continue for hours.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why a tsunami can be difficult to notice in deep ocean water is correct?

options.A: It travels very slowly in deep water
options.B: In deep water, tsunami waves may have low wave height but very long wavelengths and travel at high speeds; their height increases as they enter shallow coastal waters and slow down
options.C: It only occurs at night
options.D: It is invisible in deep water

questions.explanation: In deep water, tsunami waves may have low wave height but very long wavelengths and travel at high speeds. Their height increases as they enter shallow coastal waters and slow down.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about run-up in the context of tsunamis is correct?

options.A: The horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline
options.B: The maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land
options.C: The speed at which a tsunami travels
options.D: The time between successive tsunami waves

questions.explanation: Run-up is the maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water above a reference sea level on land.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about inundation in the context of tsunamis is correct?

options.A: The maximum vertical height reached by tsunami water
options.B: The horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline
options.C: The speed of tsunami waves in deep water
options.D: The warning system for tsunamis

questions.explanation: Inundation is the horizontal penetration of tsunami water inland from the shoreline.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the most common cause of destructive tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Ordinary wind waves
options.B: Large, shallow undersea earthquakes that cause significant vertical displacement of the seabed
options.C: Daily tides
options.D: River floods

questions.explanation: Large, shallow undersea earthquakes that cause significant vertical displacement of the seabed are the most common cause of major destructive tsunamis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how an undersea earthquake generates a tsunami is correct?

options.A: By creating strong winds over the ocean
options.B: If a large earthquake suddenly lifts or drops the seabed, it displaces the overlying water column; the disturbance generates waves that radiate outward across the ocean
options.C: By heating the ocean water
options.D: By causing the moon's gravitational pull to increase

questions.explanation: If a large earthquake suddenly lifts or drops the seabed, it displaces the overlying water column. The disturbance generates waves that radiate outward across the ocean.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether all undersea earthquakes can generate tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Every undersea earthquake generates a tsunami
options.B: Many are too small, too deep, or produce mostly horizontal displacement; tsunami generation is especially associated with large shallow earthquakes that cause substantial vertical seabed movement
options.C: Only those with magnitude above 5 generate tsunamis
options.D: Only those in the Pacific Ocean generate tsunamis

questions.explanation: Many undersea earthquakes are too small, too deep, or produce mostly horizontal displacement. Tsunami generation is especially associated with large shallow earthquakes that cause substantial vertical seabed movement.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether volcanic eruptions can generate tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Only earthquakes can generate tsunamis
options.B: Submarine or coastal volcanic eruptions, volcanic flank collapse, caldera collapse and pyroclastic flows entering the sea can displace water and generate tsunamis
options.C: Only underwater volcanoes can generate tsunamis
options.D: Only volcanoes in the Atlantic Ocean can generate tsunamis

questions.explanation: Submarine or coastal volcanic eruptions, volcanic flank collapse, caldera collapse and pyroclastic flows entering the sea can displace water and generate tsunamis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether landslides can generate tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Landslides cannot generate tsunamis
options.B: Submarine landslides or large landslides entering a water body can displace water and generate local or regional tsunamis
options.C: Only very small landslides can generate tsunamis
options.D: Only landslides in lakes, not oceans, can generate tsunamis

questions.explanation: Submarine landslides or large landslides entering a water body can displace water and generate local or regional tsunamis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether meteorite impacts can generate tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Meteorites cannot generate tsunamis
options.B: In principle, a large extraterrestrial impact into an ocean can displace water and generate tsunami waves, but such events are extremely rare
options.C: Meteorite-generated tsunamis are very common
options.D: Only small meteorites can generate tsunamis

questions.explanation: In principle, a large extraterrestrial impact into an ocean can displace water and generate tsunami waves, but such events are extremely rare.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how a submarine or coastal landslide displaces water to generate a tsunami is correct?

options.A: By heating the ocean water
options.B: A large mass moves into or beneath water, displacing water and can produce very large local waves
options.C: By creating strong winds
options.D: By changing the moon's gravity

questions.explanation: A submarine or coastal landslide involves a large mass moving into or beneath water, which displaces water and can produce very large local waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how volcanic activity generates a tsunami is correct?

options.A: Only by creating wind
options.B: Through explosion, collapse or material entering water, which displaces water and may generate local or regional tsunamis
options.C: Only by heating the ocean
options.D: Only by changing sea level

questions.explanation: Volcanic activity can generate tsunamis through explosion, collapse or material entering water, which displaces water and may generate local or regional tsunamis.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the major effects of tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Only coastal flooding
options.B: Coastal flooding and inundation, strong currents, drowning, injuries and deaths, destruction of buildings and infrastructure, erosion, saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater, damage to ports and fisheries, displacement of communities and economic disruption
options.C: Only damage to buildings
options.D: Only saltwater contamination

questions.explanation: Major effects include coastal flooding and inundation, strong currents, drowning, injuries and deaths, destruction of buildings and infrastructure, erosion, saltwater contamination of soil and freshwater, damage to ports and fisheries, displacement of communities and economic disruption.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how tsunamis can affect agriculture is correct?

options.A: They have no effect on agriculture
options.B: Saltwater can contaminate fields and groundwater, damage crops, reduce soil productivity and harm livestock
options.C: They only affect fishing, not farming
options.D: They improve soil fertility

questions.explanation: Saltwater can contaminate fields and groundwater, damage crops, reduce soil productivity and harm livestock.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how tsunamis can affect the environment is correct?

options.A: They have no environmental impact
options.B: They can erode beaches and dunes, move large amounts of sediment, damage mangroves and coastal habitats, spread debris and pollutants, and alter coastal ecosystems
options.C: They only affect marine life
options.D: They only cause temporary changes

questions.explanation: They can erode beaches and dunes, move large amounts of sediment, damage mangroves and coastal habitats, spread debris and pollutants, and alter coastal ecosystems.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why ports and coastal infrastructure are vulnerable to tsunamis is correct?

options.A: Because they are built on weak soil
options.B: Powerful currents, debris impact, flooding and rapid water-level changes can damage ships, harbours, roads, bridges, railways, power systems and communication networks
options.C: Because they are always located in earthquake zones
options.D: Because they lack warning systems

questions.explanation: Powerful currents, debris impact, flooding and rapid water-level changes can damage ships, harbours, roads, bridges, railways, power systems and communication networks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a tsunami can cause damage far inland is correct?

options.A: Tsunamis only affect the immediate coastline
options.B: The inland reach depends on wave characteristics and coastal topography; low-lying coastal plains, river mouths and bays may allow water to penetrate considerable distances
options.C: Only very small tsunamis can cause inland damage
options.D: Only in the Pacific Ocean can tsunamis cause inland damage

questions.explanation: The inland reach depends on wave characteristics and coastal topography. Low-lying coastal plains, river mouths and bays may allow water to penetrate considerable distances.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why the first tsunami wave is not necessarily the largest is correct?

options.A: Because the first wave always loses energy
options.B: A tsunami is a wave train whose waves interact with ocean-basin and coastal geometry; later waves can be larger or produce stronger currents than the first
options.C: Because the first wave is always the largest
options.D: Because later waves are always smaller

questions.explanation: A tsunami is a wave train whose waves interact with ocean-basin and coastal geometry. Later waves can be larger or produce stronger currents than the first.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami is correct?

options.A: A tsunami caused by a volcanic eruption in Indonesia
options.B: A devastating tsunami generated by the great undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004, affecting many countries around the Indian Ocean including India's east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands
options.C: A tsunami caused by a landslide in Sri Lanka
options.D: A tsunami caused by a meteorite impact

questions.explanation: A devastating tsunami generated by the great undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004. It affected many countries around the Indian Ocean, including India's east coast and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the parts of India severely affected by the 2004 tsunami is correct?

options.A: Only the west coast
options.B: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of India's eastern coastline, including Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and the Union Territory of Puducherry
options.C: Only Gujarat
options.D: Only Mumbai

questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of India's eastern coastline, including Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and the Union Territory of Puducherry, were affected, with impacts varying by location.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether the west coast of India can experience a tsunami is correct?

options.A: Only the east coast is at risk
options.B: Although exposure differs from the east coast, the west coast is not immune to tsunami hazards; tsunami risk depends on the location and characteristics of the generating event and the propagation path
options.C: Only if the tsunami originates in the Arabian Sea
options.D: Only during the monsoon season

questions.explanation: Although exposure differs from the east coast, the west coast is not immune to tsunami hazards. Tsunami risk depends on the location and characteristics of the generating event and the propagation path.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the natural warning signs of a possible tsunami is correct?

options.A: Clear skies and calm weather
options.B: A strong or long-lasting coastal earthquake, an unusual rapid rise or fall of sea level, and a loud ocean roar
options.C: Heavy rainfall and strong winds
options.D: A sudden drop in temperature

questions.explanation: A strong or long-lasting coastal earthquake, an unusual rapid rise or fall of sea level, and a loud ocean roar can be natural warning signs. People near the coast should move immediately to higher ground or inland if these signs occur.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether people should wait for an official warning after a strong coastal earthquake is correct?

options.A: Always wait for an official warning
options.B: If a person is in a coastal area and experiences strong or prolonged earthquake shaking, they should move immediately to higher ground or inland when safe to do so; do not wait for an official alert
options.C: Only wait if the earthquake is above magnitude 7
options.D: Only wait during the night

questions.explanation: If a person is in a coastal area and experiences strong or prolonged earthquake shaking, they should move immediately to higher ground or inland when safe to do so. Do not wait for an official alert.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about India's tsunami warning system is correct?

options.A: Operated by the India Meteorological Department
options.B: India's tsunami early-warning capability is operated by the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), which monitors seismic information, sea-level observations and other data to issue tsunami advisories for the Indian Ocean region
options.C: Operated by the National Disaster Management Authority
options.D: Operated by the Indian Navy

questions.explanation: India's tsunami early-warning capability is operated by the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS), which monitors seismic information, sea-level observations and other data to issue tsunami advisories for the Indian Ocean region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether a tsunami warning means the danger is over after the first wave is correct?

options.A: The danger ends after the first wave
options.B: A tsunami consists of multiple waves and strong currents may persist; people should remain in safe locations until the competent authority officially declares the threat over
options.C: The danger ends only if the first wave was large
options.D: The danger ends only in the Pacific Ocean

questions.explanation: A tsunami consists of multiple waves and strong currents may persist. People should remain in safe locations until the competent authority officially declares the threat over.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about how households should prepare before an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Only stock food and water
options.B: Secure heavy furniture and appliances; keep heavy objects on lower shelves; identify safe places; practise Drop, Cover and Hold On; prepare an emergency kit; know how to shut off gas, electricity and water if safe; maintain family communication and meeting plans; and ensure buildings follow applicable earthquake-resistant standards
options.C: Only learn first aid
options.D: Only buy a fire extinguisher

questions.explanation: Secure heavy furniture and appliances; keep heavy objects on lower shelves; identify safe places; practise Drop, Cover and Hold On; prepare an emergency kit; know how to shut off gas, electricity and water if safe; maintain family communication and meeting plans; and ensure buildings follow applicable earthquake-resistant standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what an emergency kit for earthquake preparedness should contain is correct?

options.A: Only food and water
options.B: Drinking water, non-perishable food, torch, batteries, radio or charged power bank, first-aid supplies, essential medicines, whistle and copies of important documents
options.C: Only a first-aid kit
options.D: Only a torch and batteries

questions.explanation: Keep an emergency kit with drinking water, non-perishable food, torch, batteries, radio or charged power bank, first-aid supplies, essential medicines, whistle and copies of important documents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what a person should do during an earthquake indoors is correct?

options.A: Run outside immediately
options.B: Drop, Cover and Hold On: Drop to hands and knees; take cover under a sturdy table or desk if available; protect the head and neck; hold on to the shelter until shaking stops; stay away from windows, glass, exterior walls and heavy objects; do not run outside while the building is shaking
options.C: Stand in a doorway
options.D: Use the elevator to evacuate

questions.explanation: Drop, Cover and Hold On. Drop to hands and knees; take cover under a sturdy table or desk if available; protect the head and neck; hold on to the shelter until shaking stops. Stay away from windows, glass, exterior walls and heavy objects. Do not run outside while the building is shaking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what a person should do if no sturdy table or desk is available during an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Run outside immediately
options.B: Drop near an interior wall or low, stable furniture if appropriate, protect the head and neck with the arms, and stay away from windows and objects that could fall; avoid lifts and stairways during shaking
options.C: Stand in the center of the room
options.D: Lie flat on the floor

questions.explanation: Drop near an interior wall or low, stable furniture if appropriate, protect the head and neck with the arms, and stay away from windows and objects that could fall. Avoid lifts and stairways during shaking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what a person should do outdoors during an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Stand near a building for protection
options.B: Move to an open area away from buildings, boundary walls, trees, streetlights, poles and overhead wires; stay there until the shaking stops
options.C: Lie down on the ground
options.D: Run towards the nearest tree

questions.explanation: Move to an open area away from buildings, boundary walls, trees, streetlights, poles and overhead wires. Stay there until the shaking stops.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what a person should do while driving during an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Speed up to get away quickly
options.B: Pull over carefully in a safe location away from bridges, flyovers, buildings, trees and power lines; stop, remain in the vehicle until shaking stops, and then proceed cautiously while watching for road damage
options.C: Stop immediately in the middle of the road
options.D: Get out of the vehicle and run

questions.explanation: Pull over carefully in a safe location away from bridges, flyovers, buildings, trees and power lines. Stop, remain in the vehicle until shaking stops, and then proceed cautiously while watching for road damage.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what people should do immediately after an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Return to damaged buildings to retrieve belongings
options.B: Expect aftershocks; check for injuries and provide first aid if safe; evacuate damaged buildings carefully; avoid damaged structures; check for gas leaks, fire and electrical hazards; follow official information; and avoid entering unsafe buildings
options.C: Use elevators to evacuate
options.D: Light candles to check for damage

questions.explanation: Expect aftershocks; check for injuries and provide first aid if safe; evacuate damaged buildings carefully; avoid damaged structures; check for gas leaks, fire and electrical hazards; follow official information; and avoid entering unsafe buildings.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what should be done if a gas leak is suspected after an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Light a match to check
options.B: Avoid flames and electrical switches; leave the area and report the leak; shut off the supply only if it is safe and you know how
options.C: Turn on all electrical switches
options.D: Ignore it and stay indoors

questions.explanation: If gas is suspected, avoid flames and electrical switches; leave the area and report the leak. Shut off the supply only if it is safe and you know how.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what people should do about communication after an earthquake is correct?

options.A: Make as many voice calls as possible
options.B: Use text messages where possible to reduce congestion on voice networks
options.C: Avoid all communication
options.D: Only use social media

questions.explanation: Use text messages where possible to reduce congestion on voice networks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what people near the coast should do after a strong or long earthquake is correct?

options.A: Wait for an official tsunami warning
options.B: Move to higher ground and follow tsunami evacuation instructions
options.C: Go to the beach to observe the ocean
options.D: Stay indoors

questions.explanation: If near the coast after a strong or long earthquake, move to higher ground and follow tsunami evacuation instructions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what earthquake-resistant construction is is correct?

options.A: Construction that prevents all earthquake damage
options.B: The design and construction of buildings and infrastructure to resist expected earthquake forces without unacceptable collapse or loss of life, aiming to improve structural strength, ductility, connections and overall performance
options.C: Construction that only uses wood
options.D: Construction that ignores building codes

questions.explanation: Earthquake-resistant construction is the design and construction of buildings and infrastructure to resist expected earthquake forces without unacceptable collapse or loss of life. It aims to improve structural strength, ductility, connections and overall performance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what ductility in earthquake engineering is is correct?

options.A: The ability of a material to conduct electricity
options.B: The ability of a material or structural system to undergo significant deformation beyond its elastic limit without sudden failure; ductile detailing helps structures dissipate earthquake energy
options.C: The ability of a building to float
options.D: The stiffness of a building

questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability of a material or structural system to undergo significant deformation beyond its elastic limit without sudden failure. Ductile detailing helps structures dissipate earthquake energy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about why building-code compliance is important for earthquake safety is correct?

options.A: It is only a legal requirement with no safety benefit
options.B: Building codes provide engineering requirements for design, materials, detailing and construction according to seismic hazard; proper implementation reduces collapse risk and protects life
options.C: It only applies to tall buildings
options.D: It prevents all earthquakes

questions.explanation: Building codes provide engineering requirements for design, materials, detailing and construction according to seismic hazard. Proper implementation reduces collapse risk and protects life.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what retrofitting is is correct?

options.A: The process of demolishing old buildings
options.B: The strengthening or modification of an existing building or structure to improve its resistance to earthquake shaking
options.C: The construction of new buildings
options.D: The process of predicting earthquakes

questions.explanation: Retrofitting is the strengthening or modification of an existing building or structure to improve its resistance to earthquake shaking.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about whether an earthquake can be predicted accurately is correct?

options.A: Scientists can predict the exact date, location and magnitude
options.B: Scientists can estimate seismic hazard and probabilities over time, monitor earthquakes and issue alerts after an earthquake has begun, but they cannot reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake
options.C: Scientists can predict shallow earthquakes exactly
options.D: Only volcanic earthquakes can be predicted

questions.explanation: Scientists can estimate seismic hazard and probabilities over time, monitor earthquakes and issue alerts after an earthquake has begun, but they cannot reliably predict the exact date, location and magnitude of a future earthquake.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about what an earthquake early-warning system is is correct?

options.A: A system that predicts earthquakes weeks in advance
options.B: It detects the faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source and sends alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives; it provides seconds to tens of seconds in some situations, not long-term prediction, and may not provide warning close to the epicentre
options.C: A system that prevents earthquakes from occurring
options.D: A system that only works for tsunamis

questions.explanation: An earthquake early-warning system detects the faster-arriving seismic waves near an earthquake source and sends alerts that may reach more distant locations before stronger shaking arrives. It provides seconds to tens of seconds in some situations, not long-term prediction, and may not provide warning close to the epicentre.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the correct focus and epicentre relationship is correct?

options.A: Focus is on the surface; epicentre is inside the Earth
options.B: Focus is inside Earth; epicentre is the surface point directly above it
options.C: Both are on the surface
options.D: Both are inside the Earth

questions.explanation: Focus is inside Earth; epicentre is the surface point directly above it.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares P-waves and S-waves is correct?

options.A: P-wave is shear and travels through solids only; S-wave is compressional and travels through solids and fluids
options.B: P-wave is compressional and travels through solids and fluids; S-wave is shear and travels through solids only
options.C: Both P-waves and S-waves travel through liquids
options.D: Both P-waves and S-waves are surface waves

questions.explanation: P-wave is compressional and travels through solids and fluids; S-wave is shear and travels through solids only.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares body waves and surface waves is correct?

options.A: Body waves travel along the surface; surface waves travel through Earth's interior
options.B: Body waves travel through Earth's interior; surface waves travel along or near the surface
options.C: Both travel only through the surface
options.D: Both travel only through the interior

questions.explanation: Body waves travel through Earth's interior; surface waves travel along or near the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following statements about wave arrival order is correct?

options.A: S-waves arrive first, then P-waves, then surface waves
options.B: P-waves are faster than S-waves; S-waves are faster than surface waves in typical earthquake records
options.C: Surface waves arrive first
options.D: All waves arrive simultaneously

questions.explanation: P-waves are faster than S-waves; S-waves are faster than surface waves in typical earthquake records.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Love waves and Rayleigh waves are examples of which type of wave?

options.A: Body waves
options.B: Surface waves
options.C: Sound waves
options.D: Tidal waves

questions.explanation: Love and Rayleigh waves are surface waves.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: A seismograph records ground motion; what is the record called?

options.A: Seismometer
options.B: Seismogram
options.C: Accelerograph
options.D: Epicentre

questions.explanation: A seismograph records ground motion; a seismogram is the record.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Richter magnitude is logarithmic. What does a one-unit increase represent?

options.A: Ten times energy
options.B: Ten times wave amplitude under the scale definition, not ten times energy
options.C: Two times wave amplitude
options.D: One hundred times wave amplitude

questions.explanation: Richter magnitude is logarithmic: one unit means ten times wave amplitude under the scale definition, not ten times energy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which magnitude scale is based on seismic moment and preferred for large earthquakes?

options.A: Richter scale
options.B: Moment magnitude scale
options.C: Mercalli scale
options.D: Beaufort scale

questions.explanation: Moment magnitude is based on seismic moment and is preferred for large earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which scale is location-specific and varies across the affected area?

options.A: Moment magnitude
options.B: Richter magnitude
options.C: Mercalli intensity
options.D: Seismic moment

questions.explanation: Mercalli intensity is location-specific and varies across the affected area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: India's commonly cited BIS seismic zoning system has how many zones?

options.A: Three: II, III, IV
options.B: Four: II, III, IV and V
options.C: Five: I, II, III, IV and V
options.D: Two: II and III

questions.explanation: India's commonly cited BIS seismic zoning system has four zones: II, III, IV and V.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the highest seismic zone and which is the lowest in India's four-zone scheme?

options.A: Zone I highest; Zone IV lowest
options.B: Zone V highest; Zone II lowest
options.C: Zone IV highest; Zone III lowest
options.D: Zone III highest; Zone II lowest

questions.explanation: Zone V is highest seismic hazard; Zone II is lowest in the four-zone scheme.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Karnataka includes areas in which seismic zones?

options.A: Zone I and Zone II
options.B: Zone II and Zone III
options.C: Zone IV and Zone V
options.D: Zone V only

questions.explanation: Karnataka includes Zone II and Zone III areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which agency is Karnataka's nodal agency for seismic monitoring?

options.A: KSNDMC
options.B: ISRO
options.C: NHAI
options.D: FCI

questions.explanation: KSNDMC is Karnataka's nodal agency for seismic monitoring.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which is the most common cause of major destructive tsunamis?

options.A: Ordinary wind waves
options.B: Large shallow undersea earthquakes with seabed displacement
